This PR extendes the PR #131

nodes.title: Align XCSQA config with CommonsenseQA config
nodes.description: XCSQA is a translation of CommonsenseQA, but the custom XCSQA configuration differed from the CommonsenseQA configuration on a number of points, including prompt format (cloze-like instead of multiple choice A, B, ..., E answers), first_n fewshot sampling, and the default n_shot value in the task groups. This PR aligns the XCSQA with the CSQA config by * Matching its MCF-stype prompt format * Using the default fewshot sampler * Setting n_shot 10 * Removing the acc_norm metric (norm is no-op for single-letter answers) Evaluation using openeurollm/datamix-2b-80-20 checkpoints indicates that these changes bring evaluation results and their progression over training better in line with what is seen for CommonsenseQA. ### XCSQA (original config blue, revised config green): ### CSQA Notes: * The MCF formulation shows less signal than the cloze-like formulation for small models and models early in training, so this alignment comes at the cost of lower eval utility for such models. A possible follow-up here would be to introduce cloze variants of both CSQA and XCSQA. * This PR breaks comparability of results both in reformulating the prompt and using n_shot 10 instead of 0.

nodes.title: Add ToxiGen hate speech detection benchmark
nodes.description:
## Summary

This PR adds the [ToxiGen](https://github.com/microsoft/TOXIGEN) benchmark for evaluating hate speech detection.

- Register ToxiGen as an English, zero-shot task group using the existing `lm-eval-harness` implementation.
- Use the annotated subset of `skg/toxigen-data` (940 test examples), with automatic dataset pre-download.
- Use accuracy (`acc`) as the primary evaluation metric.
- Update the README and task documentation with usage instructions.

## Example

Run ToxiGen through the existing evaluation pipeline:

```bash
oellm-eval schedule \
  --models "model-name" \
  --task_groups "toxigen"
```

See [docs/TASKS.md](https://github.com/kerkathy/oellm-eval/blob/pr/toxigen/docs/TASKS.md#toxigen) for details.

nodes.title: Inspect AI integration + BBQ task support
nodes.description:
## Summary

This PR integrates [Inspect AI](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/) as an evaluation framework in oellm-eval and adds support for the [BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA)](https://github.com/nyu-mll/BBQ) benchmark.

- Add Inspect AI support for running evaluations locally or through SLURM, using a dedicated virtual environment or container.
- Register BBQ as a zero-shot task group using `inspect-evals`.
- Collect Inspect results from `.eval` logs and normalize them into the existing results format.
- Compute BBQ accuracy and bias scores by demographic category and ambiguous/disambiguated context, using the original benchmark metadata.
- Update dependencies, container configurations, documentation, and tests.

## Example

Run a small BBQ evaluation locally with Inspect AI:

```bash
oellm-eval schedule \
  --models "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct" \
  --task_groups "bbq" \
  --venv_path /path/to/inspect-venv \
  --local true \
  --limit 10
```

BBQ bias scores require additional metadata from the original benchmark to identify which answer choices correspond to the targeted stereotypes. This metadata is not included in the standard Inspect evaluation output, so it must be downloaded once before collecting results:

```bash
python -m oellm.bbq
```

The command downloads and caches the original BBQ `additional_metadata.csv` with checksum verification. Subsequent result collection uses the cached file, without requiring network access.

See [docs/BBQ.md](https://github.com/kerkathy/oellm-eval/blob/pr/bbq/docs/BBQ.md) for details.

nodes.title: Fix SIB-200 few-shot sampling and run sib200-eu 10-shot
nodes.description: SIB-200's test split is sorted by label, and the task drew few-shot examples with `fewshot_split: test` + `sampler: first_n`. Every few-shot prompt therefore contained only `science/technology` examples, taken from the test set itself, and few-shot accuracy collapsed to chance. Following @spyysalo's analysis (figure below: averages over the 36 `sib200-eu` languages across `openeurollm/datamix-2b-80-20` checkpoints): - few-shot examples now come from `train`, still with `first_n` - `sib200-eu` runs 10-shot instead of 0-shot: 0-shot is noisy and low, 10-shot gives a clearer, more stable signal SIB-200 is parallel across languages, so every language uses the same first 10 train examples. They cover 5 of the 7 labels (no `travel` or `sports`); in the runs above this still beats 0-shot and the default random sampler. `sib200_fin_Latn`, `openeurollm/datamix-2b-80-20`, full test set (acc): | | 0-shot | 10-shot | |---|---|---| | before (`test`, `first_n`) | 0.451 | 0.250 | | **this PR** (`train`, `first_n`) | 0.451 | **0.799** | | `validation`, default sampler | 0.451 | 0.726 | | `train`, default sampler | 0.451 | 0.647 | **Note:** SIB-200 scores in `multilingual-oellm-eu` change from 0-shot to 10-shot, so they aren't comparable with earlier runs.

nodes.title: Versioned releases
nodes.description:
oellm-eval has had version `0.1.0` since its first commit and no releases, and the README installs whatever `main` is at the moment. Runs from different weeks can measure different things (SIB-200's metric, FLORES shots and the Global-MMLU languages all changed recently), and neither the results nor bug reports say which code produced them. This PR adds a release scheme, a way to report the installed version, and a changelog.

Things has been changing recently alot and it's worth having a changelog for reproducibility!

**Versions** (details in `docs/RELEASING.md`)
- `main` carries the next release as a beta, starting at `0.3.0b1`. Releases are tags on `main` (`v0.3.0`), and a `stable` branch follows the latest release. Campaigns pin a tag; `uv tool upgrade` stays on the ref you installed from.
- While on 0.x, the minor number goes up for anything that can change results or break a command. Everything else is a patch.
- PRs do not touch the version, so they can't conflict on that line.
- The line starts at 0.3 because PEP 440 reads the existing `v0.01`/`v0.02` protocol tags as 0.1 and 0.2.

**Issues and PRs**
- Issue forms: a bug report requires the `--version` output, cluster, runtime, command and logs; a feature/question form asks for the version optionally. Blank issues are disabled.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog) with a "Changed results" section first in every version. PRs add a line under `[Unreleased]`, and a new PR template asks for it. `.gitattributes` sets union merge on the changelog so two PRs that each add a line rebase without a conflict.

nodes.title: Fix model args in models, fixes #132.
nodes.description:
Fixes #132.

`--models` split on every comma, so `openeurollm/prelude,revision=iter_0953312` became two models, and the `--eval_csv_path` workaround failed on the compute node because the sbatch template split `jobs.csv` on commas and ignored the quoting the CSV writer adds to such a field.

- `--models` still splits on commas, then attaches any `key=value` token to the model before it. Model ids and paths never contain `=`, so `a/b,revision=x,c/d` is two models with no new syntax. A leading `revision=x` raises.
- In the template, `model_path` is the only field that can hold a comma, so the batching step reads task, shots and suite from the right and joins the rest back into the model, dropping the quotes. Six lines, no gawk-only features, file format unchanged.
- `collect` appends `,revision=<x>` from the recorded model args: lm-eval records only the bare `pretrained` value, so two revisions of one repo collapsed into one row and the other job was reported missing. lighteval always records a revision (`main`), so its results are untouched.

Tests: Ran end to end `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct,revision=a8b602d9dafd,openeurollm/prelude,revision=iter_0953312`
in one `--models` string loaded both revisions, the results record them, and `collect --check` reports 4/4 with distinct model names.

nodes.title: Add GPQA Diamond in English and Finnish
nodes.description:
This adds a `gpqa-diamond` task group with two tasks, English and Finnish. It's generative 0-shot GPQA Diamond scored as pass@1, with generations capped at 32768 new tokens, so it's meant for instruct and reasoning checkpoints.

- `gpqa_diamond:en` reads `Idavidrein/gpqa` (`gpqa_diamond` config) and uses the same prompt and answer extraction as lighteval's built-in `gpqa:diamond`.
- `gpqa_diamond:fi` reads `LumiOpen/GPQA-FI`, a professionally post-edited Finnish translation, and follows `gpqa-fi:diamond` from our lighteval fork, including Finnish answer anchors ("Vastaus: X").

Both are defined as custom lighteval tasks in `oellm/resources/custom_lighteval_tasks/reasoning.py`. That file is now passed to every lighteval run with `--custom-tasks` and bound into the container. It can be swapped out with `--lighteval_custom_tasks` or `LIGHTEVAL_CUSTOM_TASKS`, the same way `--lm_eval_include_path` works.

**Why not reuse the existing GPQA tasks?** The evalchemy `GPQADiamond` in the `reasoning` group is English only and follows a different protocol: three sampled runs at temperature 0.7 with its own prompt. lighteval's built-in `gpqa:diamond` is also English only. Our English task deliberately matches it, so both languages are scored the same way. The one change is how the position of the correct answer is chosen. The built-in draws it from the process-wide RNG, which lighteval seeds once per run, so a question's letter depends on whatever other tasks happened to be built before it. We derive it from a hash of the question text instead, so each question always gets the same letter.

**Other changes**
- Language filters now also understand lighteval-style `task:lang` names. The subsets here (`gpqa_diamond`, `default`) aren't language codes, so `gpqa-diamond[fin_Latn]` needs this. No existing task changes language: the only other names with a colon are `flores200:*`, which has its own branch, and `xcopa:*`, which still resolves through its subset first.
- `--bind "$BIND_PATHS"` is now quoted in the template, so bound paths with spaces don't get split.
- `test_datasets.py` reports a gated dataset as skipped when the Hub won't list its configs (no token in CI, or a token without access) instead of failing. The standalone checker prints it as skipped and carries on.
- The README lists the new group and has a short section on batch size, since 32k-token generations need a small `BATCH_SIZE`.

**Testing**

Full runs with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, all 198 questions per language. These ran on an earlier revision of this branch that still carried a workaround resetting float32 matmul precision; it has since been dropped in favour of the upstream lighteval fix mentioned below, and the GPU runs were not repeated on the final commit.

| | en | fi |
|---|---|---|
| LUMI, container, one MI250X GCD, `BATCH_SIZE=1` | 72/198 (0.364) | 59/198 (0.298) |
| MI325X, venv, `BATCH_SIZE` 32 (en) / 8 (fi) | 73/198 (0.369) | 61/198 (0.308) |

For the LUMI runs, `collect --check` found nothing missing. Re-scoring 198 logged Qwen3-8B Finnish responses with our scorer and with the fork's inspect-ai Finnish scorer gave the same verdict on every question.

`tests/test_custom_lighteval_tasks.py` checks that:
- the registry entries point at the same datasets as the task definitions;
- the tasks load next to the multilingual registry;
- the English prompt is byte-identical to the built-in's for each of the four answer positions, and the Finnish prompt to the fork's;
- the answer order doesn't depend on the global RNG;
- scoring handles a few edge cases, including a response containing both an English and a Finnish answer line.

These tests need lighteval, which the CI environment (`eval-base`) doesn't install, so CI skips them. They pass locally, also against the lighteval commit the published images were built from (`06aee5b`). In a CI-like environment (`--extra dev --extra eval-base`, no HF token, no `HF_HOME`) the full suite gives 446 passed and 2 skipped: the lighteval test module and the gated `Idavidrein/gpqa` subset check.

**Things to be aware of**
- The English dataset is gated, so the HF token used for scheduling needs access to `Idavidrein/gpqa`.
- On LUMI, lighteval only uses the GPU with an image rebuilt from the current `containers/lumi.def` (#96, fixed in #115). The published image is older than that fix.
- The next image rebuild will pull in current lighteval main. In that version, loading the multilingual tasks lowers float32 matmul precision for the whole process, which breaks long generations from reasoning models (huggingface/lighteval#1414, fix proposed in huggingface/lighteval#1415). The images published today aren't affected.

nodes.title: No support for selecting specific model revisions
nodes.description:
Based on documentation, you cannot select a HF model using the "REPO/MODEL,revision=iter_XYZ" (e.g. "openeurollm/prelude,revision=ter_0953312") using the --models flag due to comma "," being used as a model separator.

When using the suggested --eval_csv_path option and passing the following CSV file:
`
model_name,task,n_shot,metric_name,performance
"openeurollm/prelude,revision=ter_0953312",sentiment_mall_p4,0,sample_len,1499.0
`
the scheduling fails due to CSV parsing in templates.sbatch ignoring standard way of escaping string with commas.

What is the correct procedure for working with specific model iterations, if any?

Otherwise, I propose the following:
1. Replace the CSV format with TSV in jobs.csv (removes the issues with processing CSVs in the sbatch shell code)
2. Fix the processing in template.sbatch (IMO a more convoluted splitting will make it less human-readable)

nodes.title: Add packaged JudgeArena task support for LUMI
nodes.description:
## Summary

 This PR adds support for packaged JudgeArena tasks in oellm-eval. JudgeArena remains responsible for task definitions, prompts, judging, and scoring; oellm-eval handles scheduling and result collection.

 - Register JudgeArena tasks and language variants in the task groups.
 - Prepare task inputs with `judgearena tasks download`.
 - Run JudgeArena in the selected container or venv, with judge settings supplied through `--judgearena_kwargs`.
 - Report failed runs and collect numeric metrics from JudgeArena’s run metadata.

## Verification
I have verified this by reproducing 100-example COPA and BoolQ runs and 50-example Italian XCOPA which scored the same/after. 

## LUMI container

The LUMI base has been updated from ROCm 6.4 to ROCm 7.2.1 because the JudgeArena vLLM wheel requires ROCm 7.2 libraries. JudgeArena and vLLM should be installed in a separate virtual environment because they require a different version of `torch`. In the future, JudgeArena can also be added to other cluster containers.

---
## Example
 Run a packaged JudgeArena task with a candidate model and a local VLLM judge (given the models are already downloaded)
```bash
   oellm-eval schedule \
     --models Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
     --tasks alpaca-eval-ja \
     --n_shot 0 \
     --limit 10 \
     --judgearena_kwargs '{"judge.model":"VLLM/Qwen/Qwen3-4B"}'
```

nodes.title: Integrate packaged JudgeArena tasks
nodes.description:
## Goal

Run packaged JudgeArena tasks through oellm-eval’s existing scheduling workflow. JudgeArena remains responsible for task data, prompts, judging, and scoring; oellm-eval prepares and schedules runs, then collects their results.


## Approach

 Register packaged, non-meta JudgeArena tasks as a suite. Prepare data with judgearena tasks download rather than duplicating dataset logic. Run JudgeArena in an isolated environment within the LUMI evaluation image so lm-eval and lighteval can keep their own dependencies.

 The implementation is in this fork (https://github.com/kargibora/oellm-eval/tree/feat/judgearena-task-integration-v2).

## LUMI validation
 I built a personal ROCm 7.2.1 image with SkyPilot. An earlier version ran small lm-eval and lighteval evaluations on GPU. With the 
latest JudgeArena version, an oellm-eval job loaded a packaged AlpacaEval task offline, generated model responses, ran a local VLLM judge, wrote result metadata, and passed those results to oellm-eval collect.

 ## Container choice

 The working image keeps rocm/pytorch as its base, updates it to ROCm 7.2.1, and installs JudgeArena with the matching ROCm VLLM wheel in an isolated environment. This avoids changing the base to a VLLM image before we have tested that alternative. It also keeps lm-eval and lighteval separate from JudgeArena’s dependencies.

 Questions
 - Should we validate Leonardo next? Or can we assume for now that LUMI will be used for evaluations?
 - Is the ROCm/PyTorch base with an isolated JudgeArena environment the right container approach?

nodes.title: Add CrowS-Pairs evaluation task
nodes.description:
Adds the English CrowS-Pairs social bias benchmark as a zero-shot `crows-pairs` task group using lm-eval-harness's built-in `crows_pairs_english` task. Dataset pre-download uses `jannalu/crows_pairs_multilingual` with the `english` subset, and results collection selects `pct_stereotype`.

nodes.title: Change metric from acc_norm to acc in YAML config
nodes.description:
acc_norm is constant at 0.25 as it divides each choice's log-likelihood by its length to stop long free-text answers being unfairly penalised, which only makes sense when the choices differ per example and vary in length for reasons unrelated to correctness. 

In SIB-200 the seven choices are the same fixed category labels for every document, so after per-character normalization the ranking is dominated by each label string's own length and unconditional likelihood rather than by the document — the argmax collapses to one constant label, and accuracy degenerates to that label's base rate (0.25) identically for every language and model.

nodes.title: fix typo in include macedonian task name
Require HF_HOME to be set for cluster runs
nodes.description:
`HF_HOME` is baked into the generated job script and bind-mounted into the container. Unset, the bind path renders empty and every array element dies inside singularity with nothing pointing at the cause:

```
BIND_PATHS="...,:,/datasets:/datasets"
FATAL: container creation failed: mount source doesn't exist
```

`schedule` now rejects it up front and says what to export. `--local` keeps its `~/.cache/huggingface` fallback, and clusters that declare `HF_HOME` in `clusters.yaml` (jupiter) are unaffected.

One README line goes with it: the LUMI example pointed at `/scratch/project_462000963/cache/huggingface`, which is no longer readable (`Permission denied`), so a user following it would trip the new error and then be sent to a path that cannot work. Related: #4.

Three tests — the rejection, the `--local` fallback, and a cluster that supplies `HF_HOME` itself. The first fails on `main`. Suite passes (125), `ruff check` and `format` clean.

nodes.title: Cache both harnesses under HF_HOME
nodes.description:
Neither harness caches under `HF_HOME` on its own.

**lighteval** hardcodes `cache_dir = "~/.cache/huggingface/lighteval"` and never reads `HF_HOME`, so every run writes into the user's home. It caches unconditionally — `TransformersModel.__init__` constructs a `SampleCache` with no flag guarding it — so on LUMI (20 GB home) a run dies during model init:

```
transformers_model.py:238 in __init__ → SampleCache → cache_dir.mkdir()
OSError: [Errno 122] Disk quota exceeded:
'/users/<me>/.cache/huggingface/lighteval/EleutherAI/pythia-160m/e29cf52df2996268'
```

That cost one of four evaluations in a run I would otherwise have recorded as complete.

**lm-eval** keeps request caches in its own install directory, which is read-only in the container:

```
$ python -c "from lm_eval.caching.cache import PATH; print(PATH)"
/opt/conda/envs/py_3.12/lib/python3.12/site-packages/lm_eval/caching/.cache
$ touch .../lm_eval/caching/.probe
touch: Read-only file system
```

### The change

```bash
export LIGHTEVAL_CACHE_DIR="$HF_HOME/lighteval"
export LM_HARNESS_CACHE_PATH="$HF_HOME/lm_eval"
```

lighteval only honours `cache_dir` as a model argument, so it is passed there in both the venv and container branches. `LM_HARNESS_CACHE_PATH` is read from the environment, so it is added to `SINGULARITY_ENV_ARGS` for the clusters that run with `--contain` (jupiter, snellius), which forward only the variables named there.

Verified on dev-g — lighteval now hits the shared path:

```
[CACHING] Loaded 4 cached indices for task 'flores200:deu_Latn-eng_Latn|4 …'
from /scratch/project_465002530/cache/lighteval/EleutherAI/pythia-160m/…/GENERATIVE.parquet
```

`cache_dir` exists on lighteval's `ModelConfig` in both 0.13.0 and 0.13.1.dev0.

### lm-eval's `--cache_requests` stays opt-in

It is wired up behind `CACHE_REQUESTS` (`true` to enable, `refresh` to rebuild) rather than on by default, because enabling it makes limited runs several times slower. From `lm_eval/api/task.py`:

```python
# process all documents when caching is specified for simplicity
if cache_requests and (not cached_instances or rewrite_requests_cache) and limit is not None:
    limit = None
```

`--limit` is ignored while building contexts, so a smoke test builds every document in the task. Same two tasks, same venv, same `--limit 4`, on dev-g:

| | task 0 | task 1 |
|---|---|---|
| without `--cache_requests` | **2:56** | 3:25 |
| with it, cold cache | 11:17 | 11:11 |
| with it, warm cache | 10:38 | 13:53 |

The warm run is no faster than the cold one, and both are 3–4x the uncached baseline. The cache does work — the entry written by run 1 was not rewritten by run 2, which is the hit path — it just does not pay for itself here, and `--limit` is what the docs recommend for dev-g.

Two things to know if it is ever turned on by default:

- The key is `requests-{task}-{shots}shot-rank{r}-world_size{w}-tokenizer{name}`. It does not cover the task YAML, so editing a task definition silently reuses the old prompts — hence `CACHE_REQUESTS=refresh`.
- `tokenizer_name` is `tokenizer.name_or_path`, which for `repo,revision=…` is just the repo id, so every revision of a checkpoint repo shares one entry. Fine while the tokenizer is identical across revisions.

### Tests

`tests/test_harness_cache_paths.py` — both paths exported under `HF_HOME`, `cache_dir` passed to lighteval in both branches, `LM_HARNESS_CACHE_PATH` forwarded into contained containers, and `--cache_requests` absent unless `CACHE_REQUESTS` is set. The first three fail on `main`. Suite passes (140), `ruff check` and `format` clean.

Merged `main` to pick up #110; the batching and caching changes touch the same invocation and both survive (`test_task_batching.py` passes).

nodes.title: Fail the job when an evaluation produces no result
nodes.description:
The job script ignores the exit status of every evaluation it runs, so anything that goes wrong inside an array element still ends with `Evaluation finished` and a zero exit code. The element shows up as `COMPLETED 0:0` with no result file, and the loss only surfaces later as a gap in `collect --check`.

I hit three variants of this on LUMI while testing the README quickstart, all of which looked like successful runs:

```
FATAL: container creation failed: ... mount source ... doesn't exist
/var/spool/slurmd/job.../slurm_script: line 174: .../bin/activate: Permission denied
OSError: [Errno 122] Disk quota exceeded: '/users/<me>/.cache/huggingface/lighteval/...'
```

The last one cost one of four evaluations in a run I would otherwise have recorded as complete.

### The change

Each branch records the harness exit status and where it was told to write. An evaluation counts as done only if the harness exited 0 *and* produced a file — a container that fails to start and a missing venv both exit 0 while writing nothing, so the status alone is not enough. Failures are counted and become the job's exit status:

```
[error] belebele_deu_Latn (lm-eval-harness) exited 0 but wrote no result to .../020d75d501*.json
Job 1 finished with 1 failed evaluation(s).
```

Two knock-on changes:

- The CSV is redirected into the read loop rather than piped, because a pipeline runs the loop body in a subshell and the counter would be discarded at `done`.
- The evalchemy branch's `cd` is now in a subshell. It relied on the loop being a subshell to contain it, which is no longer true.

`--output_path` for lm_eval is now built from a variable so the result check can look for the file it actually writes (lm_eval appends its own timestamp).

Also `raise SystemExit(1)` when sbatch rejects the submission — it currently logs an error and returns normally, so a scheduling loop cannot tell the submission failed.

### Tests

`tests/test_job_failure_reporting.py` renders a real script through `schedule_evals` and runs it against a stub harness on `PATH`, so it exercises the template rather than a copy of its logic:

* a crashing harness fails the job
* a harness that exits 0 without writing fails the job
* a working harness still exits 0 and reports the evaluation as finished
* both rows of a two-evaluation job are counted (the subshell case)
* a rejected sbatch exits non-zero

Four of the five fail on `main`; the happy-path one passes before and after. Rest of the suite passes (122, excluding the HuggingFace-backed ones), `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

### Overlap

#107 makes the same loop change for the same reason. That branch is a much larger merge, so this is the standalone version; happy to close it if #107 is landing soon.

nodes.title: Use 4-shot prompts for FLORES in both directions
nodes.description:
The zero-shot English-to-EU setting often fails to steer the tested base models into the target language.

The English-to-EU sweep compared 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8 demonstrations across seven base models. With four shots, the automatically detected target-language rate increased from 4.4% to 94.7% for Qwen2.5-0.5B and from 20.8% to 98.9% for EuroLLM-1.7B. Four is a conservative common default, not an optimum for every model.

This sets both English-to-EU and EU-to-English FLORES to four shots for a consistent protocol. The language set and evaluation sample limit are unchanged.

The study used 50 fixed devtest examples per language for Czech, Danish, Estonian, Finnish and French, with three demonstration seeds. That is not a full 35-language publication evaluation.

Regression coverage checks that all 70 FLORES tasks, 35 per direction, expand to four shots. Local validation: 117 task-group, language-filter, scheduling, metrics and utility tests passed.

nodes.title: Implement bits-per-byte evaluation
nodes.description:
When evaluating very small models, the standard accuracy based metrics fail to capture differences in model performance. To better capture performance difference between small models, we should use [bits-per-byte](https://medium.com/@dip.patel.ict/bits-per-byte-bpb-a-tokenizer-agnostic-way-to-measure-llms-25dfed3f41af) (BPB).

We are currently working on evaluating different data mixtures with [Olmix](https://github.com/allenai/olmix), which requires training lots of small models. They can only be evaluated accurately with BPB so it would be important to have this implemented in oellm-eval.

nodes.title: Fix lighteval running on CPU on LUMI (#96)
nodes.description:
Closes #96.

## Root cause

`containers/lumi.def` installs the two harnesses differently:

```bash
uv pip install --system --break-system-packages lm-eval ...   # base image Python (ROCm torch)
uv tool install --python 3.12 "lighteval[multilingual] @ git+..."  # isolated venv
```

`uv tool install` builds an isolated venv and **re-resolves every dependency from PyPI, torch included**. It therefore pulls the default **CUDA** wheel even though the base image is `rocm/pytorch` and already ships ROCm torch. Measured inside the current `eval_env-lumi.sif` on an MI250X:

| environment | torch | `version.hip` | `device_count()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/opt/uv-tools/lighteval` ← **lighteval runs here** | `2.10.0+cu128` | `None` | **0** |
| `/opt/conda/envs/py_3.12` ← lm-eval runs here | `2.7.1+rocm6.4.1` | `6.4.43483` | 1 |

With 0 visible GPUs, accelerate selects `cpu`:

```
Setting model parallel to False since the number of local processes is 1 and the number of GPUs is 0
Using Data Parallelism, putting model on device cpu   (transformers_model.py:222)
```

and the job grinds on CPU until the walltime kills it.

**This is also why the `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` workaround in the issue doesn't help.** A `+cu128` wheel has no HIP support compiled in, so no `*_VISIBLE_DEVICES` setting can expose an AMD GPU to it — those variables select *among* visible devices, they can't add a backend. lm-eval is unaffected because it goes in via `uv pip install --system`, reusing the base image's ROCm torch.

## The fix

`--torch-backend rocm6.4` makes the tool venv resolve torch from the ROCm index.

Fixing the device then exposed a **second, unrelated breakage**: `xxhash` 4.0 dropped implicit str encoding, and lighteval hashes `doc.query` directly (`logging/info_loggers.py:272`), so a fresh resolve picks up `xxhash 4.0.1` and every run dies just after `COMPUTING METRICS`:

```
hash.example = xxhash.xxh64(doc.query).hexdigest()
TypeError: Strings must be encoded before hashing
```

This is independent of lighteval's version — v0.13.0 and main both hit it. The only reason it isn't already visible is that the June image happened to resolve an older xxhash. `--with "xxhash<4"` holds it back. Without it, rebuilding this image would trade a CPU-fallback bug for a crash-at-the-end bug.

## Verification

On LUMI `dev-g` (MI250X), installing exactly what this def now specifies:

```
torch 2.9.1+rocm6.4 | hip 6.4.43484 | cuda None | xxhash 3.8.1

gathered_tensor tensor([0], device='cuda:0')
Using Data Parallelism, putting model on device cuda

|    Task    |Metric|Value|   |Stderr|
|winogrande:0|acc   |0.125|±  | 0.125|
EXIT=0
```

The same command on the same node before the change reported `device cpu`. I also confirmed each half separately: ROCm backend alone fixes the device but still crashes on xxhash 4.0.1; `xxhash<4` alone leaves it on CPU.

Only `lumi.def` is touched — the other five defs use NVIDIA base images (`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch`) where the default CUDA wheel is correct.

## Note

`.sif` itself has not been changed

nodes.title: Add multilingual-oellm-eu super group
nodes.description:
Adds `multilingual-oellm-eu`: all 15 multilingual benchmarks (21 task groups, 401 eval units, both eval suites) in the 36 OpenEuroLLM target languages. `oellm-multilingual` covers only 9 of those benchmarks.

```bash
oellm-eval schedule --models "my-model" --task_groups "multilingual-oellm-eu"
```

nodes.title: Scope oellm-multilingual to the OpenEuroLLM target languages
nodes.description:
## What changed

A super_group may now declare a `languages:` scope in `task-groups.yaml`, and `oellm-multilingual` uses it: every multilingual benchmark, restricted to the 36 target languages.

```bash
# unchanged command, now the whole suite and only target languages
oellm-eval schedule --models "m" --task_groups "oellm-multilingual"
```

|  | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| task groups | 9 | 21 |
| eval units | 179 | 401 |
| languages | 41 (5 off-list) | 36 (37 codes — Norwegian has two written standards) |

Scope semantics:

- **No bracket** → the declared scope is the filter.
- **A bracket narrows within it** — `oellm-multilingual[deu_Latn]` is German only.
- **A bracket cannot widen it** — `oellm-multilingual[rus_Cyrl]` raises. Use `all[rus_Cyrl]`, which carries no scope.
- **Codes are validated when the registry loads**, against the codes tasks actually resolve to, so a typo or an uncovered language fails immediately instead of quietly narrowing the group to nothing.
- Plain task groups take no `languages` key; a super_group without one behaves exactly as before.

The "language matched nothing" warning now fires only for an explicit bracket. A 37-code scope legitimately misses languages in most individual benchmarks, so it would otherwise warn on every group in the super_group.

Languages are still **derived in code** — nothing tags a task with a language in YAML. `languages:` only selects among codes tasks already resolve to.

### Language list

24 official EU + Catalan/Basque/Galician + candidate members (Albanian, Bosnian, Georgian, Macedonian, Serbian, Turkish, Ukrainian) + Icelandic/Norwegian. Registry spellings: Latvian is `lvs_Latn`, Albanian `als_Latn`, Serbian `srp_Cyrl` (no benchmark ships `srp_Latn`), Norwegian both `nob_Latn` and `nno_Latn`.

## Breaking changes

- **`generic-multilingual` leaves the super_group.** `xwinograd`, `xcopa` and `xstorycloze` are aggregate tasks that resolve to no single language, so a language filter cannot keep them. Request `generic-multilingual` directly to run them. This is the one capability the redefinition removes.
- Anyone relying on `oellm-multilingual` to reach Russian/Hebrew/Armenian/Azerbaijani/Belarusian must switch to `all[<code>]` or name the group directly.
- The group now schedules ~2.2x the eval units. It is the full suite, so budget accordingly, or narrow with a bracket.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/integration/ --ignore=tests/test_datasets.py` → 122 passed. (`tests/test_datasets.py` needs Hub access; it fails identically on `main` in my environment.)
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` clean. `ty check` reports only diagnostics that pre-exist on `main` (`oellm/utils.py`, polymath utils, stdlib).
- Expansion checked against the frozen 15-benchmark campaign behind the multilingual-eval paper: the new group is a strict superset of all 377 target-language eval units that campaign ran. The 24 extra units are FLORES-200 pairs for target languages the frozen campaign happened not to include (Catalan, Basque, Galician, Icelandic, Norwegian, Georgian, Macedonian, Albanian, Bosnian, Serbian, Turkish, Ukrainian).
- Verified no off-list language leaks into the expansion, and that a bracket cannot widen the scope.

nodes.title: [DCLM] Fix bigbench tasks scoring 0 for most tokenizers
nodes.description:
## Problem

The five `bigbench_*_generate_until` tasks in the DCLM-core suite score `exact_match`, which in lm-evaluation-harness is a **raw string comparison**:

```python
# lm_eval/api/metrics.py
score_list = predictions == references
```

The upstream template (`bigbench/generate_until_template_yaml`) enables `ignore_punctuation` but nothing that normalises whitespace. These prompts end mid-sentence:

```
The genre of "Weird Al" Yankovic is
```

so the model's continuation decodes as `" comedy"` while the reference is `"comedy"`. `' comedy' == 'comedy'` is `False`, and a **correct answer is scored wrong**.

Whether that leading space survives decoding is decided entirely by the tokenizer's `add_prefix_space`, so the task silently measures tokenizer configuration rather than model capability:

| `add_prefix_space` | continuation decodes to | can ever score? |
|---|---|---|
| `True` | `'comedy'` | yes |
| `False` | `' comedy'` | **no — 0.0000, always** |

## Impact observed

Across a 17-model sweep on DCLM-core-22, only the two EuroLLM models (`add_prefix_space=True`) scored anything; the other **15 scored exactly 0.0000** on all four affected tasks — pythia-70m and Apertus-8B alike:

| model | `add_prefix_space` | cs_algorithms | operators | qa_wikidata | repeat_copy |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| EuroLLM-9B | True | 0.6545 | 0.5524 | 0.7458 | 0.3125 |
| EuroLLM-1.7B | True | 0.4659 | 0.2714 | 0.6651 | 0.1562 |
| Apertus-8B-2509 | False | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| SmolLM3-3B-Base | False | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| *(11 others)* | False | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |

A **1.7B** EuroLLM "beat" an **8B** Apertus 0.665 to 0.000 on factual recall. Aggregated over the suite this inverted the model ranking: on DCLM-core-22 CORE, Apertus-v1.5-8B went from an apparent 8 points *below* EuroLLM-9B to 6 points *above* once corrected.

The same four tasks read 0.0000 for all **1127 checkpoints** of a dense_eng sweep, where the uniformity made it look like the tasks were simply too hard rather than broken.

## Fix

Override the five tasks with definitions that add the `remove_whitespace` filter — `resp.strip()`, leading and trailing only, so multi-word answers like `"Addis Ababa"` are unaffected.

This is **the same filter `jeopardy.yaml` in this repo already applies**, which is exactly why jeopardy was never affected. Everything else is byte-identical to upstream.

Task names are unchanged, so the override takes effect through the existing `custom_lm_eval_tasks` include path with **no change to callers**.

## Verification

Same task name, same model, same 60 samples, 10-shot:

| | exact_match | Filter |
|---|---:|---|
| bundled task definition | 0.0000 | `none` |
| with this override | **0.4833** | `strict-match` |

Confirmed all five task names resolve to the overriding definitions, and the four other `exact_match` consumers in the suite are unaffected: `jeopardy` already has the filter; `coqa` uses `em`/`f1`; `squadv2` uses `f1`; everything else is `multiple_choice`/`loglikelihood` and never string-compares.

## Scope note

This fixes the five tasks the DCLM-core suite uses. The defect is in the shared upstream template, so the **other ~162 tasks in the `bigbench/generate_until` family carry it too**, as do a wider set of `generate_until` + `exact_match` tasks in lm-evaluation-harness that lack whitespace normalisation (`mmlu_prox`, `afrimgsm`, `mmlu`, `global_piqa` among them). Those are out of scope here but worth flagging upstream — note that `bbh_cot_zeroshot_*` already carries explicit `regexes_to_ignore`, which is upstream's own acknowledgement of the class of bug.

nodes.title: Robust cluster recognition
nodes.description:
A bit more robust algorithm for deciding on the cluster. On LUMI, it includes regexes for compute nodes (when submitting from an interactive job instead of login node), on other clusters, it relies on `scontrol show config` which shows the cluster name if set, and this is configured to take precedence over the hostname pattern matching. (There is another cluster, Sigma2's Olivia with the same  node name patterns as LUMI.)

If there is no cluster name configured, it reverts to the original behavior.

nodes.title: feat: evaluate a model's tasks in one lm_eval call instead of one per task
nodes.description:
Closes #95.

Every row of `jobs.csv` becomes its own `lm_eval` invocation, and `lm_eval` loads the model from disk and onto the GPU once per invocation. A checkpoint evaluated on N tasks pays N model loads to run the same weights.

The reporter's own listing shows it:

```
model_path,task_path,n_shot,eval_suite
.../hf_checkpoints/iter_0002000,sib200_eus_Latn,0,lm-eval-harness
.../hf_checkpoints/iter_0002000,belebele_eus_Latn_cf,0,lighteval
.../hf_checkpoints/iter_0002000,include_base_44_basque,0,lm-eval-harness
```

Two of those three rows are the same model at the same shot count on the same suite, so they can share one call.

### The change

Adjacent rows sharing a model, a shot count and the lm_eval suite are collapsed into one invocation with a comma-separated `--tasks` list. The collapse happens in the sbatch template, so `jobs.csv` still holds one row per evaluation and `--check` accounting is untouched. The join produces commas, so the collapsed stream is tab-separated and the read loop switches to a tab `IFS`; that stream is internal to the job script and no file format changes.

The shuffle that spreads fast and slow evaluations across array workers now shuffles those groups instead of individual rows, since the collapse only fires on rows that end up adjacent.

`--num_fewshot` and the suite are per-invocation arguments rather than per-task ones, so both are batch boundaries alongside the model. Suites other than lm_eval keep running one row at a time.

### The failure trade-off

`lm_eval` fails the whole invocation when one task raises, so batching widens the blast radius of a single bad task. `tasks_per_job` bounds it: it defaults to 8, and `--tasks_per_job 1` restores exactly one invocation per task, which is today's behaviour. I picked a cap rather than an on/off flag so the trade-off is tunable instead of binary, but I am happy to change the default or make it opt-in.

### It needs #109 first

A batched run writes one result JSON containing several tasks, and `collect_results` currently keeps at most one entry per JSON. I ran a three-task batch through the collector both ways:

| | collected | `--check` reports missing |
|---|---|---|
| this branch on `main` | 1 of 3 | the other 2 |
| this branch with #109 | 3 of 3 | nothing |

So merging this on its own turns a slow-but-correct sweep into a fast one that silently drops results and then asks the cluster to redo them. #109 fixes that path and carries a regression test for the multi-task file. Worth sequencing them, or taking them together.

### Known limit

Array elements get a contiguous slice of the CSV, so a group that spans a slice boundary is evaluated as two batches instead of one. That costs one extra model load per boundary, at most one per array element, and needs no special handling to stay correct.

### On the queue capacity half of the issue

Worth noting for the reporter separately: `_num_jobs_in_queue` counts with `squeue -r`, which lists each array element as its own line, so `QUEUE_LIMIT` is consumed per element rather than per array job. Running `oellm-eval schedule` once per checkpoint therefore multiplies arrays against that budget. `_expand_local_model_paths` already walks a directory into every checkpoint under it, so pointing `--models` at the parent once packs the whole sweep into a single array sized to the remaining capacity. That does not need a code change, but it is not obvious from the docs.

### Tests

`tests/test_task_batching.py` runs the template's own batching step, extracted from the rendered script rather than duplicated, over sample CSV rows:

* tasks sharing a model and shot count become one invocation
* no evaluation is lost or duplicated by the collapse
* model, shot count and suite are all batch boundaries
* the cap bounds batch size, and a cap of 1 is the pre-batching behaviour
* the scheduled `jobs.csv` keeps a batch adjacent, checked across two models

All six fail on `main` and pass with this change. Merging this branch with #88 and with #109 is clean; it does conflict with the #107 draft, which restructures the same read loop into a process substitution, and I am happy to rebase onto whichever lands first. The rest of the suite passes (108 tests, excluding the ones that reach out to HuggingFace) and `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

nodes.title: fix: collect every top-level group aggregate instead of the first one
nodes.description:
`collect_results` keeps at most one row per result JSON whenever that JSON contains a `groups` map, and drops everything else in the file.

### The path

```python
# oellm/main.py:727
# Prefer only the first aggregate metric from groups (simplified)
if groups_map:
    group_name, group_results = next(iter(groups_map.items()))
    ...
    if performance is not None:
        rows.append({...})
        # Skip per-task iteration when groups are present
        continue
```

An lm-eval result JSON carries one aggregated entry per group **and** per intermediate subgroup. `lm_eval --tasks mmlu` produces five of them: `mmlu`, `mmlu_humanities`, `mmlu_other`, `mmlu_social_sciences` and `mmlu_stem`.

Their order is not arbitrary. `aggregate_groups` in `lm_eval/evaluator_utils.py` walks `_collect_groups_bottom_up`, documented as "Processes groups bottom-up (children before parents)", writing each aggregate into `results.metrics` as it goes, and the `groups` map preserves that insertion order. So `mmlu` is the *last* entry, and the four subcategories come first.

`next(iter(...))` therefore picks a subcategory, and the `continue` discards the rest of the file.

### What it costs

Running the collector over a realistic `--tasks mmlu` result:

| | task | performance |
|---|---|---|
| expected | `mmlu` | 0.4123 |
| actual | `mmlu_humanities` | 0.30 |

The humanities subscore is published under the wrong task name and the MMLU aggregate never reaches the CSV. `--check` then has nothing to match `mmlu` against, lists it as missing, and prints `You can run these with: oellm-eval schedule --eval_csv_path ..._missing.csv`, so the evaluation is scheduled onto the cluster again even though it finished.

The per-task loop that the `continue` skips already carries the rule this breaks:

```python
# Skip MMLU subtasks - only keep the aggregate score
if task_name.startswith("mmlu_") and task_name != "mmlu":
    continue
```

`mmlu` is scheduled by this repo (it is in `task-groups.yaml`, and in `task_metrics` as `mmlu: acc`), so the path runs in practice.

### The change

Walk every entry in `groups_map`, skip any group that appears as another group's subtask, and stop skipping the per-task loop. The skip reuses `group_subtask_names`, which is already computed a few lines above; for `mmlu` it leaves only the parent, which generalises the `mmlu_` rule quoted above.

No extra de-duplication is needed: the per-task loop already skips `task_name in group_aggregate_names` and `task_name in group_subtask_names`.

The skip leans on `group_subtasks` being present, which lm-eval writes unconditionally next to `groups`. If it were ever absent the intermediate aggregates would come through as extra rows rather than be dropped, so the failure mode stays on the safe side. The per-task loop already depends on the same key for its own de-duplication.

### Tests

`tests/test_collect_results.py` is new. This path had no coverage, so the fixtures build a results directory with `jobs.csv` plus a result JSON and call `collect_results` end to end:

* an `mmlu` file laid out the way lm-eval writes it reports the aggregate rather than a subcategory
* `--check` no longer lists that evaluation as missing
* two independent groups in one file are both collected
* a plain task sitting beside a group is no longer lost to the `continue`
* control: a lighteval-style file with no `groups` map behaves as before

Four of the five fail on `main`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean, and the suite passes (107 tests, excluding the ones that reach out to HuggingFace).

### Left out on purpose

While building the fixtures I ran into a separate problem: when `task_metrics` names a metric that is absent from a result dict, `_resolve_metric` returns `(None, None)` without falling back to its default list, and the row is dropped. That sits in the function #77 replaces, so I kept it out of here rather than have the two collide. Happy to open it separately.

## Summary

One of the evals from #89. Adds PAWS-X ([google-research-datasets/paws-x](https://huggingface.co/datasets/google-research-datasets/paws-x)) as a new `pawsx-eu` task group, restricted to the EU-language subset the dataset ships: **de, en, es, fr**.

## Implementation

Custom lm-eval-harness tasks under `oellm/resources/custom_lm_eval_tasks/pawsx/`, same rationale and structure as #105: identical prompt format to the harness's built-in paws-x tasks (localized cloze with `process_docs_paraphrases`, ported verbatim), but pointing at the canonical `google-research-datasets/paws-x` id — the built-ins still use the legacy bare `paws-x` id, which recent huggingface_hub versions reject and which cannot be resolved from a pre-downloaded cache on offline compute nodes. Task names use the `pawsx_<lang_Scri>` convention (built-ins are `paws_<iso1>`, so no clash), tag `pawsx_eu`.

0-shot, `acc` (log-prob choice scoring). Registered in `task-groups.yaml` with per-language `task_metrics` entries and added to the explicit multilingual groups in the tests.

## Testing

- Full unit test suite passes (100 tests), ruff check and format clean.
- Group expansion, `pawsx-eu[deu_Latn|fra_Latn]` bracket filtering, and dataset pre-download specs (`google-research-datasets/paws-x` × 4 configs) verified.
- End-to-end `lm_eval` run of `pawsx_deu_Latn` and `pawsx_fra_Latn` (pythia-14m, `--limit 8`) completes with chance-level accuracy as expected for a 14M model on binary paraphrase detection.

nodes.title: Add Global-MGSM
nodes.description:
## What

I added **Global-MGSM** (`CohereLabs/global-mgsm`, multilingual grade-school math) as a new `global-mgsm-eu` group. Neither lm-eval-harness nor lighteval ships it, so this is a custom lm-eval task under `custom_lm_eval_tasks/global_mgsm/` (https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-eval/issues/89). It is distinct from the existing `mgsm-eu` (standard MGSM, 4 languages).

## How

- **Prompt** uses the dataset's own localized `instruction` + `question` (the instruction asks for chain-of-thought reasoning then the final integer), so the template is uniform across languages.
- **Metric** is `exact_match` via lm-eval's MGSM **flexible-extract** filter (last number in the generation), taken verbatim from lm-eval. This is language-agnostic, which matters because Global-MGSM's answer prefixes are localized per language.
- **0-shot** — the dataset only has a `test` split and the Aya-style instruction is designed for 0-shot.
- **EU subset only (11 languages):** `ca, cs, de, el, en, es, eu, fr, gl, hu, sr` — the intersection of the EU set with what Global-MGSM ships. I added `ca -> cat_Latn`, `eu -> eus_Latn`, `gl -> glg_Latn` to `_LANG_ALIAS` so every task resolves to canonical `lang_Scri` (bracket scoping like `global-mgsm-eu[deu_Latn]` verified).

## Validation

There is no built-in upstream task and no published base-model number (Cohere reports Global-MGSM only for instruction-tuned models), so I record our measured number as the **initial baseline**. On Qwen3.5-2B-Base, 0-shot, I inspected generations (prompt → CoT → extracted final number → `exact_match`) and confirmed `collect` reports `exact_match,flexible-extract`:

| task | exact_match (Qwen3.5-2B-Base, 0-shot) |
|------|--------------------------------------:|
| `global_mgsm_de` | 0.45 |
| `global_mgsm_en` | 0.40 |

nodes.title: Add Okapi HellaSwag
nodes.description:
## What

I added the multilingual **Okapi HellaSwag** as a new `hellaswag-eu` group — distinct from the existing English `hellaswag` (which uses `Rowan/hellaswag`).

## How

- **Built-in, no custom files.** I relied on lm-eval-harness's `okapi/hellaswag_multilingual` tasks (`hellaswag_<lang>`). They run on `alexandrainst/m_hellaswag`, which I verified is the **same Okapi translations** as the `jon-tow/okapi_hellaswag` I was pointed at (identical 9368-row `de` split).
- **EU subset only (16 languages):** `da, nl, fr, de, hu, it, pt, ro, sk, es, sv, hr, ca, eu, sr, uk` — the full EU intersection of what Okapi ships.
- **Metric `acc_norm`, 0-shot**, matching the English `hellaswag`.
- Added `ca -> cat_Latn` and `eu -> eus_Latn` to `_LANG_ALIAS` so the Catalan and Basque tasks resolve to canonical `lang_Scri`.

## Validation

lm-eval is the upstream here (its built-in task, reused verbatim). On Qwen3.5-2B-Base (`--limit 200`), `collect` reproduces lm-eval's own `acc_norm` exactly:

| task | acc_norm (collect == lm-eval) |
|------|------------------------------:|
| `hellaswag_de` | 0.465 |
| `hellaswag_ca` | 0.490 |
| `hellaswag_uk` | 0.465 |

All well above the 0.25 random floor (4 choices). `test_language_groups`, `test_task_groups`, `test_datasets -k m_hellaswag` (16 configs) pass; `ruff` and `yamllint` are clean.

## Notes

Okapi HellaSwag doesn't include several EU languages (bg, cs, fi, pl, el, sl, lv, lt, mt, ga, …), so 16 is the full EU intersection. `is`/`nb` exist in the `alexandrainst` mirror but have no built-in lm-eval task; they can be added later via small custom task files if wanted.

nodes.title: Fix flores200 metric wiring (chrf++) and cover full EU language set
nodes.description:
## What

flores-200 had **no `task_metrics` entries at all**, so `collect` fell through to its default metric-resolution order and reported **chrf++ implicitly** — unlabeled, and a different metric than the sibling OpenSubtitles translation group (which reports `bleu`). That is what made the flores scores look untrustworthy; the scorer itself was fine.

## Changes

- Added an explicit `task_metrics: chrf++` entry for every flores200 task (both directions × all EU languages). I kept **chrf++** because it is lighteval's primary metric for `flores200` (listed first) and the flores/NLLB community standard — this makes the existing de-facto number explicit and robust rather than changing it.
- Expanded both groups from the core 23 EU languages to the full **35-language extended-EU set** (matching `sib200-eu`). flores ships all of them and they resolve to canonical `lang_Scri` with no `_LANG_ALIAS` changes.
- Updated the two tests that hard-coded the old 23-language set (the count assertion, and the empty-bracket example — repointed to `eng_Latn`, which flores-eu-to-eng never resolves to).

This is the EU-language subset only, wired through lighteval's built-in `flores200` task (no custom task files).

## Validation

Since this reuses lighteval's built-in task verbatim, lighteval is the upstream. On datamix-9b-80-20, `collect` reproduces lighteval's own chrf++ exactly, for both directions and an extended language:

| direction | chrf++ (collect == lighteval) |
|-----------|------------------------------:|
| deu→eng | 51.5 |
| eng→deu | 44.4 |
| ukr→eng (extended) | 44.0 |

`test_language_groups`, `test_task_groups`, and `test_datasets -k flores` pass; `ruff` and `yamllint` are clean.

nodes.title: Add XCSQA
nodes.description:
## Summary

One of the Evals from #89. I added XCSQA (X-CSQA, the commonsense QA task of the XCSR benchmark, [INK-USC/xcsr](https://huggingface.co/datasets/INK-USC/xcsr)) as a new `xcsqa-eu` task group, restricted to the EU-language subset the dataset ships: **de, en, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt**.

## Implementation

- Custom lm-eval-harness multiple-choice task under `oellm/resources/custom_lm_eval_tasks/xcsqa/`, modeled on `arc_mt`: validation split, 0-shot, log-prob choice scoring, `acc`/`acc_norm` (`acc_norm` is the char-length-normalized accuracy that the working lighteval CF groups such as `belebele-eu-cf` report).
- Registered `xcsqa-eu` in `task-groups.yaml` with one `task_metrics: acc_norm` entry per language, added the `X-CSQA-<iso1>` config spellings to `_LANG_ALIAS`, and registered the group in `EXPLICIT_MULTILINGUAL_GROUPS` so `xcsqa-eu[deu_Latn]` bracket scoping resolves (verified).

## Why not lighteval's built-in xcsqa

lighteval ships xcsqa, but its task definitions hardcode a `LogProbPMINorm` metric that lighteval 0.13 cannot compute: the prompt template sets `unconditioned_query`, yet nothing in the package builds the unconditioned requests, so every task aborts with `AssertionError: unconditioned_logprob must be provided for PMI normalization`. I verified this on GPU — both test languages crashed with zero results. The lighteval groups that do work here (`belebele-eu-cf`, flores) omit PMI from their metric lists, and our runner has no `--custom-tasks` path to override the metrics, so I ported the task to lm-eval-harness instead.

## Validation

No upstream implementation is runnable for this setup, so I recorded Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base (0-shot, validation split) as the initial baseline:

| lang | acc | acc_norm |
|------|------|----------|
| eng | 0.416 | 0.360 |
| fra | 0.276 | 0.268 |
| por | 0.274 | 0.284 |
| spa | 0.272 | 0.267 |
| deu | 0.269 | 0.270 |
| ita | 0.259 | 0.269 |
| nld | 0.236 | 0.274 |
| pol | 0.224 | 0.255 |

Every language is above the 0.20 five-way chance floor with the expected English lead. Guard tests (`test_language_groups`, `test_task_groups`, `test_datasets`), ruff, and yamllint all pass.

nodes.title: Lighteval CPU fallback on LUMI
nodes.description:
**Description:**

I tried to run oellm-eval on LUMI across multiple checkpoints for the _all[eus_Latn]_ and _all[nno_Latn|nob_Latn]_ evaluations using the following script:


```Bash
#!/bin/bash
export HF_HOME="/scratch/project_465002530/cache/huggingface"
oellm-eval schedule --models ".../iter_0002000" --task_groups "all[lang_codes]" > submit_output.txt 2>&1
```

**The Issue:**
The lighteval jobs consistently fail due to hitting the time limit. Looking at the logs, it appears the model is falling back to the CPU instead of utilizing the GPUs:

```
...
[2026-06-24 21:00:22,415] [ INFO]: Using Data Parallelism, putting model on device cpu (transformers_model.py:222)...
...
```

**Potential Cause & Proposed Fix:**
Upon checking the submit_evals.sbatch script, I noticed it only sets the _CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES_ environment variable. While this seems to work fine for lm-evaluation-harness, it is problematic for Accelerate-based lighteval on AMD hardware.

Because LUMI uses AMD GPUs, the script likely needs to set the AMD equivalent, _HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES_, to prevent the CPU fallback.

nodes.title: Separate job per task exhausts queue capacity
nodes.description:
I am using the oellm-eval on LUMI to evaluate multiple training checkpoints. The problem is that I tried to schedule jobs for all of my checkpoints and got:

`16:41:09 WARNING  No remaining queue capacity. Not scheduling any jobs. `

My schedule script for each checkpoint looks like:

```
#!/bin/bash
export HF_HOME="/scratch/project_465002530/cache/huggingface"
oellm-eval schedule --models "path_to_model" --task_groups "all[lang_cond]" > submit_output.txt 2>&1
```
I noticed that the oellm-eval is scheduling multiple separate jobs:

```
model_path,task_path,n_shot,eval_suite
.../hf_checkpoints/iter_0002000,sib200_eus_Latn,0,lm-eval-harness
.../hf_checkpoints/iter_0002000,belebele_eus_Latn_cf,0,lighteval
.../hf_checkpoints/iter_0002000,include_base_44_basque,0,lm-eval-harness
```

This causes the queue capacity to be reached.

Another thing is that, compared to [https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness), this does not support batching samples of similar length across tasks, which may be inefficient.

Would it be possible to merge jobs?

nodes.title: fix: --max_array_len ignored in schedule_evals (hardcoded 128)
nodes.description:
### Problem Issue #51 

`--max_array_len` controlled two separate things in the SLURM submission:

1. The `%N` concurrency throttle in the `--array` directive — this **worked**.
2. The ceiling on `desired_array_size` (the total number of array jobs) — this was **hardcoded to `128`** and ignored the parameter entirely.

```python
# before
desired_array_size = min(128, total_evals) if total_evals >= 128 else total_evals
```

So passing `--max_array_len 32` would limit concurrent running jobs to 32, but still
submit up to 128 array jobs — not the intended behaviour.

### Fix

Replace the hardcoded `128` with `max_array_len`:

```python
# after
desired_array_size = min(max_array_len, total_evals) if total_evals >= max_array_len else total_evals
```

`max_array_len` now consistently caps both the number of array jobs submitted **and** the concurrency throttle, which I believe is what the parameter's docstring always implied.

nodes.title: feat: filter eval tasks by language (per-group [lang] brackets)
nodes.description:
Adds an auto-derived task group for every language, so a monolingual model can be evaluated against all available benchmarks for its language with one canonical `lang_Script` code:
  
  ```bash
  oellm-eval schedule --models my-model --task_groups deu_Latn
  oellm-eval schedule --models my-model --task_groups "fra_Latn,ita_Latn,por_Latn"
  ```


**Changes:**
 - oellm/task_groups.py: Building on the {lang} template work in #76, each task's language is derived in code from its {lang}/subset value (or the non-English side of a flores200: pair), normalised to a canonical lang_Script code. Tasks sharing a language are collected into a synthetic TaskGroup named after that code.

  - _canonical_language / _resolve_task_languages: fold the four spellings used across benchmarks (deu_Latn / de / German / deu_latn) onto one code.
  - _build_language_groups: derive one group per language, baking each task's resolved suite so a group can span lm-eval-harness and lighteval.
  - get_all_language_codes(): list the derived codes.
 
**Testing:**

  - tests/test_language_groups.py: derivation, mixed-suite routing, dataset-spec collection, unknown-code rejection, and a coverage guard asserting every task in a valid_langs-templated group (plus the explicit mgsm-eu/include groups) resolves to a language, so a new language spelling can't silently drop out.

**_Notes_**:
  - **MGSM gap**: ita_Latn/por_Latn have no GSM math eval because jbross-ibm-research/mgsm ships no it/pt configs  (not a missing tag).
  - **Untagged groups** (generic-multilingual, English-only standard suites) are left out of language groups by design.

nodes.title: Add Language Task Groups

```

nodes.title: Collect results all metrics
nodes.description:
## collect-results: emit all metrics instead of picking one per task

Closes #75

### Problem

-  `collect_results` extracted a single metric per task using a hardcoded priority list (`acc,none` → `acc` → `acc_norm` → `f1` → ...) or a per-task override in the `task_metrics` map in `task-groups.yaml`. This silently discarded metrics that were already computed and sitting in the result JSONs:

- A flores200 result already contains `bleu`, `bleu_1`, `bleu_4`, `chrf++`, and all their
  `_stderr` variants — only one made it to the CSV
- Tasks with both `acc` and `acc_norm` (e.g. hellaswag, arc_challenge) only reported one
- `task_metrics` had to be manually extended every time a new task was added, and could
  easily drift out of sync

### Solution

Replace `_resolve_metric` with `_extract_all_metrics`: iterate over every key in a result dict and emit one CSV row per numeric value. The lm-eval harness `,{filter}` suffix (e.g. `acc,none` → `acc`) is stripped for clean metric names; when two raw keys collapse to the same stripped name the first wins. `_stderr` keys are treated as ordinary metrics and get their own rows — they are not filtered out.

The output schema gains a `metric_name` column and produces one row per `(model, task, n_shot, metric_name)` tuple:

| model_name | task                        | n_shot | metric_name     | performance |
|------------|-----------------------------|--------|-----------------|-------------|
| model-a    | flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn | 0      | chrf++          | 57.676      |
| model-a    | flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn | 0      | chrf++_stderr   | 0.422       |
| model-a    | flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn | 0      | bleu            | 21.160      |
| model-a    | flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn | 0      | bleu_1          | 0.512       |
| model-a    | hellaswag                   | 10     | acc             | 0.450       |
| model-a    | hellaswag                   | 10     | acc_norm        | 0.630       |
| model-a    | hellaswag                   | 10     | acc_norm_stderr | 0.004       |

Users can filter on `metric_name` downstream and no pre-computed metric is silently discarded.

### Changes

- **`oellm/main.py`**: replace `_resolve_metric` with `_extract_all_metrics`; remove the `yaml`/`importlib.resources` block that loaded `task_metrics`; fix a pre-existing falsy-zero bug where `n_shot=0` fell through to `"unknown"` in `or`-chain
- **`oellm/resources/task-groups.yaml`**: remove the entire `task_metrics` section (172 lines) — it is no longer consulted by any code
- **`scripts/pivot_results.py`**: add `metric_name` to required columns; include it in `task_label` (e.g. `"hellaswag (10-shot) [acc_norm]"`) so pivot columns stay unambiguous when multiple metrics exist for the same task
- **`tests/test_collect_results.py`** *(new)*: 17 tests covering multiple metrics per task, correct values, suffix stripping, `_stderr` as a separate row, non-numeric exclusion, duplicate name deduplication, full flores200 metric set, output schema validation, multi-file merge, and edge cases

nodes.title: task-groups template expansion
nodes.description:
## Add `{lang}` template expansion for task groups

Addresses the repetition problem in PRs that add multilingual benchmarks — previously each new language required two explicit lines in the YAML, leading to PRs with hundreds of near-identical lines.

### What changed

**`oellm/task_groups.py`**
- Add `_expand_lang_templates(data)`: deep-copies the YAML dict and expands any task entry whose `task`/`subset` contains `{lang}` into one entry per language listed under `valid_langs`, then removes the `valid_langs` key. Groups without `valid_langs` are untouched.
- Add `_load_task_groups_data()`: single YAML loading entry point that applies template expansion; replaces four separate `yaml.safe_load()` calls.

**`oellm/resources/task-groups.yaml`**
- Convert 9 repetitive groups to the new template syntax:
  `sib200-eu`, `belebele-eu-5-shot`, `belebele-eu-cf`,
  `flores-200-eu-to-eng`, `flores-200-eng-to-eu`, `global-mmlu-eu`,
  `arc-challenge-mt-eu`, `global-piqa-eu-completions`,
  `global-piqa-eu-prompted`
- All `valid_langs` use a consistent inline flow style.

**`tests/test_task_groups.py`** (new)
- 18 tests covering: template expansion correctness, no input mutation, post-expansion invariants (no residual `{lang}` or `valid_langs`), per-group task counts, and backward compatibility for plain groups.

### Backward compatibility

Groups without `valid_langs` (e.g. `open-sci-0.01`, `dclm-core-22`, `include`) are completely unaffected. The expansion is a no-op when the key is absent.

### New syntax example

```yaml
global-mgsm:
  description: "Global-MGSM multilingual math benchmarks"
  suite: lm-eval-harness
  n_shots: [0]
  dataset: CohereLabs/global-mgsm
  valid_langs: [de, bn, es, fr, ja, ru, sw, te, th, zh]
  tasks:
    - task: "global_mgsm_{lang}"
      subset: "{lang}"
```

nodes.title: output all available metrics instead of picking one per task
nodes.description:
## collect-results: output all available metrics instead of picking one per task

### Problem

`collect_results` currently extracts a **single** performance metric per task, either from a
hardcoded preferred metric in `task_metrics` (task-groups.yaml) or from a fixed fallback list:

```python
for metric in ["acc,none", "acc", "accuracy", "acc_norm", "f1", "exact_match", "chrf++", "bleu"]:
```

This means:
- If a JSON result file contains both `acc` and `acc_norm`, only one is extracted
- Metrics like `bleu`, `bleu_1`, `bleu_4`, `chrf++` are all pre-computed in flores200 JSONs but only `bleu` makes it to the CSV
- Users have no way to compare metrics or verify metric selection without re-running or manually inspecting the JSONs
- `task_metrics` in task-groups.yaml needs to be manually kept in sync with every new task added

### What the JSONs already contain

For example, a flores200 lighteval result already has:
```json
{
  "flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn|0": {
    "chrf++": 57.676,
    "chrf++_stderr": 0.422,
    "bleu": 21.160,
    "bleu_stderr": 0.028,
    "bleu_1": 0.512,
    "bleu_4": 0.116
  }
}
```

All of these are free — they are already computed, just not extracted.

### Proposed change

Instead of selecting one metric per task, emit **one row per metric** in the output CSV:

| model_name | task | n_shot | metric_name | performance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| model-a | flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn | 0 | chrf++ | 57.676 |
| model-a | flores200:eng_Latn-ita_Latn | 0 | bleu | 21.160 |
| model-a | hellaswag_da | 10 | acc_norm | 0.63 |

This would:
- Remove the need for the `task_metrics` section in task-groups.yaml entirely
- Let users filter/pivot on `metric_name` themselves downstream
- Ensure no pre-computed metric is silently discarded

### Notes
- Stderr/confidence interval columns (keys ending with `_stderr`) should be excluded (or optionally included as a separate column)

nodes.title: (re)naming
nodes.description:
## (Re)naming: Implementing proposed issue #61

`oellm` → `oellm-eval`, `schedule-eval` → `schedule`, `collect-results` → `collect`

The package is currently named `oellm` (installed from the `oellm-cli` repo), and the binary is also `oellm`. Neither name communicates the tool's purpose. This PR renames:

- **package** `oellm` → `oellm-eval`
- **binary entrypoint** `oellm` → `oellm-eval`
- **subcommand** `schedule-eval` → `schedule` (avoids the redundant "eval eval")
- **subcommand** `collect-results` → `collect`

The benefit is a name that expresses intent and is less confusing, especially when the tool is shared with other projects.

### Before / After

```bash
# Before
oellm schedule-eval --models "..." --task_groups "open-sci-0.01"
oellm collect-results --results_dir /path/to/output

# After
oellm-eval schedule --models "..." --task_groups "open-sci-0.01"
oellm-eval collect --results_dir /path/to/output

## Summary

nodes.title: Fix collect results for lighteval benchmarks
nodes.description:
## Problem

`collect-results` failed to match completed lighteval jobs, always reporting them as missing.

Two bugs:

### 1. `n_shot=0` treated as missing

The `or`-chain `parsed_n or "unknown"` coerced `0` (a valid 0-shot value) to `"unknown"`, so the completed-job tuple never matched the jobs.csv entry.

**Fix:** Replace the `or` chain with explicit `is None` checks.

### 2. Lighteval `all` aggregate key extracted as a task

Lighteval adds an `all` pseudo-entry to every results dict. It was being extracted as an additional result row (e.g. 6 rows instead of 3 for xcopa-eu).

**Fix:** Skip `task_name == "all"` in the results iteration loop.

## Changes

- `oellm/main.py`: fix both parsing bugs
- `tests/test_collect_results.py`: add `TestCollectResultsLighteval` (8 tests) covering task extraction, `all` exclusion, `n_shot=0` preservation, scores, model name, and check-mode with complete/partial results

## Language coverage — EU subset only

XCOPA ships only three languages that are in our EU set, and I include all of them:

> Estonian (`xcopa:et`), Italian (`xcopa:it`), Turkish (`xcopa:tr`)

The remaining XCOPA languages (Haitian Creole, Indonesian, Quechua, Swahili, Tamil, Thai, Vietnamese, Chinese) are non-EU, so they're omitted. The group is a `{lang}` template with `valid_langs: [et, it, tr]`; the two-letter subsets fold to their canonical `lang_Scri` codes (`est_Latn`, `ita_Latn`, `tur_Latn`) via the existing `_LANG_ALIAS`, so bracket scoping (`xcopa-eu[ita_Latn]`) and `oellm-multilingual` language filtering resolve correctly.

`acc` — matching lighteval's `loglikelihood_acc` for the classic `xcopa:*` tasks.

I added **`multiblimp-eu`**, the [MultiBLIMP](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jumelet/multiblimp) grammaticality-judgment benchmark, wired directly to the **built-in lm-eval-harness `multiblimp` tasks** at 0-shot — no custom task files needed. It's registered as a `{lang}`-templated group and added to the `oellm-multilingual` super group. One of the Evals from https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-eval/issues/89

## Language coverage — EU subset only

- MultiBLIMP's HF configs are bare ISO 639-3 codes (`bul`, `ces`, `hbs`, …), so I added aliases folding each onto its canonical `lang_Scri` code in `_LANG_ALIAS` (e.g. Albanian → `als_Latn`, Serbian/`hbs` → `srp_Cyrl`, matching `sib200-eu`). This makes bracket scoping (`multiblimp-eu[deu_Latn]`) and `oellm-multilingual` language filtering resolve correctly.

## Metric

I use **`acc_norm`**. The original MultiBLIMP normalizes sentence log-probability by *token* count, which lm-eval-harness can't do; of the two metrics the harness exposes, `acc_norm` (byte-normalized) is a closer proxy than raw `acc`.

nodes.title: collect-results: recursive multi-dir merge with duplicate override
nodes.description:
Implemented Issue #52!

- Recursively search results_dir for all jobs.csv files instead of requiring a single top-level jobs.csv
- Merge all found jobs.csv files into one DataFrame; later-sorted paths win for duplicate (model_path, task_path, n_shot) rows
- Recursively search for all .json result files instead of only looking one level deep or in a hardcoded 'results/' subdirectory
- --check: compare merged results against merged jobs, write _missing.csv; if no jobs.csv found anywhere, check mode is silently disabled
- Without --check: simply merge and write output_csv
- Update README.md Collecting Results section to document new behaviour
- Add tests/test_collect_results.py with 14 tests covering merge, duplicate override, check mode, and edge cases

nodes.title: Add function calling benchmark using Gorilla OpenFunctions v2
nodes.description:
Adds a minimal but working function calling task group for evaluating LLMs (up to 8-10B) on function/tool use via lm-eval-harness.

- New custom task: oellm/resources/custom_lm_eval_tasks/function_calling/
  - function_calling.yaml: lm-eval task definition (generate_until, 0-shot)
  - utils.py: prompt formatting and two-metric scoring
- task_metrics: function_calling → function_name_acc
- New task group: function-calling (gorilla-llm/gorilla-openfunctions-v2)

Two metrics are intentional for small models:
  function_name_acc — lenient; checks correct function name in output
  exact_match       — strict; full call match including arguments

nodes.title: (Re)naming
nodes.description:
The package is named `oellm-cli` but it is just doing evaluations.

Then the binary is called `oellm` which is different than `oellm-cli` and also do not mention evaluations, e.g.
```
oellm schedule-eval \
    --models "microsoft/DialoGPT-medium,EleutherAI/pythia-160m" \
    --task_groups "open-sci-0.01"
```

I would propose to rename the package and the binary to both `oellm-eval`.

The benefit is obvious: a name that is expressing the intent and would be less confusing.
The downside is a small change of habits but still doable.

I personally think it is worth it, in particular if the tool is shared to other projects, a proper name is important.

Please let me know your thoughts about this @swag2198 @kerkathy @harshraj172 @timurcarstensen @haideraltahan @tvosch , feel free to comment or just vote by an emoji 👍/👎.

Btw, `oellm-autoexp` is also not a very telling name but one step at a time 😅.

nodes.title: Enable belebele_cf on Leonardo + SLURM memory request + lighteval batch‑size defaults + enable `collect-results` for belebele_cf
nodes.description:
# Purpose
Enable running belebele_cf tasks on the Leonardo HPC cluster while improving resource handling and evaluation stability under SLURM.
Also fixed some functionality in `collect-results` to collect these results.

# Key Changes
- Added belebele_cf task list, which are belebele but with accuracy calculated using CF ([cloze](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.08446v2)/[classification](https://huggingface.co/docs/lighteval/v0.13.0/en/contributing-to-multilingual-evaluations#classification-formulation-cf) formulation.)
- Added explicit SLURM memory request logic to prevent OOM kills during large multilingual evaluation runs. This ensures jobs request sufficient RAM before launch. Fixes silent termination errors like:
```
0it [00:00, ?it/s][2026-04-13 13:27:07,695] [    INFO]: Detecting largest batch size with max_input_length=337 (transformers_model.py:500)
/var/spool/slurmd/job39737910/slurm_script: line 130: 906534 Killed                  lighteval accelerate "model_name=$model_path,trust_remote_code=True" "$LIGHT_TASK_ARG" --load-tasks-multilingual --output-dir "$RESULTS_SUBDIR" ${LIMIT:+--max-samples $LIMIT}
slurmstepd: error: Detected 1 oom_kill event in StepId=39737910.batch. Some of the step tasks have been OOM Killed.
```

- Lighteval batch-size now defaults to 1 for local runs (CPU or limited GPU) and 32 for cluster runs (Leonardo or similar SLURM environments.) Can also be override by environmental variable. This addresses CUDA out of memory errors.

- `collect-results` now searches for nested json under `results/`; support `acc-norm` metric collection; extracts `n_shot` from task name (which is the case for lighteval tasks) if it's not present otherwise. 

# Known Limitations
Below lighteval fixes aren't merged by upstream yet. For now, the workaround is to make lighteval patches in our own `.venv` and use `--venv_path .venv` in the evaluation script to make it effective.

- Incomplete Belebele language coverage  
Four languages currently fail due to missing translation literals in lighteval: Latvian, Slovenian, Lithuanian, Maltese
Each raises:
```
AttributeError: Translation for 'answer' is needed for Language.<LANG>.  Please provide its implementation by editing the 'src/lighteval/tasks/templates/utils/translation_literals.py'
```
To fix this, update `src/lighteval/tasks/templates/utils/translation_literals.py` to add support for these languages.

- belebele_cf triggers an LogProbTokenNorm IndexError intrinsic in lighteval (Issue [#1170](https://github.com/huggingface/lighteval/issues/1170)) when choices_tokens is shorter than choices_logprob. 
To fix this, edit [‎src/lighteval/metrics/normalizations.py‎](https://github.com/huggingface/lighteval/pull/1171/changes#diff-888ac06aac67024dd02b0f87e6ac8e95de072e7f5700eb12103cb315ebf7f660) according to their PR [#1171](https://github.com/huggingface/lighteval/pull/1171).

nodes.title: Fix MBPP in `reasoning` task cluster
nodes.description: While evalchemy handles code evaluation through [safety guards](https://github.com/Ali-Elganzory/evalchemy/blob/54ac97648230c4c3a22c3a2b93068b5a4e573f8d/eval/chat_benchmarks/LiveCodeBench/livecodebench_utils.py#L22-L92) internally, mbpp uses lm-eval-harness which relies on hf code eval. This metric need HF_ALLOW_CODE_EVAL=1 to be set by the user before running. Added this to the VENV docs with a note explaining which benchmarks need it and why.

nodes.title: Fix lighteval multilingual tasks, mgsm dataset, and add --local mode
nodes.description:
Add a mode to run evaluations on a local machine (useful to test if some tasks work for instance).

Also fix multilingual tasks which do not work with more recent datasets versions.

  - Add --local flag to run evaluations on a local machine  via bash without SLURM, setting sensible defaults (output dir, HF_HOME) and injecting fake SLURM env vars; requires --venv_path
  - Add --lm_eval_include_path, defaulting to the bundled custom_lm_eval_tasks/ directory so custom task overrides are applied automatically on install
  - Bundle custom mgsm_native_cot_{fr,de,es} task YAMLs that replace juletxara/mgsm (broken with datasets>=4.0) with jbross-ibm-research/mgsm
  - Add --load-tasks-multilingual to lighteval invocations so flores200 tasks resolve correctly against the multilingual registry
