nodes.title: Feature Request: Merge CSV Results from Multiple `schedule-eval` Runs
nodes.description:
### Motivation
When running evaluations with `oellm schedule-eval`, each run creates a new directory named by timestamp, e.g. `<eval_dir>/2026-03-12-18-22-42`

Example usage:

```bash
# Run evaluations using a task group
oellm schedule-eval \
    --models "microsoft/DialoGPT-medium,EleutherAI/pythia-160m" \
    --task_groups "open-sci-0.01"
```

Then results are collected into a CSV:
```bash
oellm collect-results \
    --results_dir <eval_dir>/2026-03-12-18-22-42 \
    --check \
    --output_csv results.csv
```

This workflow works well when running one large sweep. However, in practice evaluations are often run incrementally (e.g., new models added later).

### Problem

Currently there is no built-in way to merge results from multiple evaluation directories. This means:
•	If a new model is evaluated in a separate run, its results are isolated in a different folder.
•	To create a single unified CSV, users must manually merge files.
•	Previously computed results may be recomputed unnecessarily.

### Proposed Feature

Add functionality to merge results from multiple evaluation folders, e.g.:

```bash
oellm collect-results \
    --results_dirs <eval_dir>/2026-03-12-18-22-42,<eval_dir>/2026-03-13-10-01-22 \
    --output_csv merged_results.csv
```

or

```bash
oellm collect-results \
    --results_dirs <eval_dir>
    --output_csv merged_results.csv
```

### Desired Behavior

1. Deduplicate entries using a key such as: (model_name, task, n_shot, metric_name)
2. Combine results from multiple evaluation directories.
3. If duplicates exist, keep the most recent result (based on folder timestamp or file modification time).
4. Produce a single merged CSV.

nodes.title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflows for code quality
nodes.description:
## Summary
This PR adds GitHub Actions workflows to enforce code quality standards across the project.

## Changes
- **Main CI workflow** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
  - Runs on pushes to main and pull requests
  - Tests against Python 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, and 3.11
  - Uses Ruff for both code formatting and linting
  - Includes YAML linting with yamllint
  - Includes shell script linting with ShellCheck
  - Type checking with mypy (non-blocking for now)

- **Pre-commit workflow** (`.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml`)
  - Automatically runs pre-commit hooks on pull requests
  - Ensures consistent code style before merging

- **Ruff configuration** in `pyproject.toml`
  - Line length set to 88 characters
  - Configured with common linting rules (pycodestyle, pyflakes, isort, etc.)
  - Consistent formatting preferences

- **Pre-commit configuration** (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`)
  - Standard file checks (trailing whitespace, EOF, large files, etc.)
  - Ruff for automatic fixing of linting issues
  - Mypy for type checking

## Benefits
- Consistent code formatting across all contributions
- Early detection of common code issues
- Automated import sorting
- Type safety checks
- Protection against common file issues (large files, merge conflicts, etc.)

## Testing
The workflows will run automatically once this PR is merged. Contributors can also run `pre-commit install` locally to get instant feedback before pushing.

nodes.title: feat(dllm): AR-to-block-diffusion conversion for Qwen3 with ablation suite
nodes.description:
Block-wise discrete diffusion (BD3/SDAR-style) continued pretraining for Qwen3 models that start
from the official pretrained AR checkpoints (Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B/8B-Base, configs for 14B), on top
of MegaDLMs:

- `oellm_autoexp/dllm/`: a launcher (`pretrain_block_difflm.py`) that subclasses the MegaDLMs
  difflm GPTModel. Input `[xt, x0]` of length 2L, RoPE position `i mod L` for both copies, a
  FlexAttention block-diffusion mask passed through a module-level context, and loss on the noisy
  copy only (optional token shift, ELBO or uniform weighting, complementary masking, clipped noise,
  block-size schedule, document mask, an AR control objective, and a deterministic validation
  NELBO).
- An NLD-style hybrid objective `nld` (spec section 15): AR cross entropy on a token-causal clean
  stream plus 0.3 x block diffusion with B = 32, the first 20 percent of the iterations AR-only.
  The clean stream stays an exact AR model, so an nld checkpoint is evaluated both as a diffusion
  model (M1-M3) and in AR mode (exact NLL, `<run>.m1_ar.json`); the exporter records the clean
  attention (`dllm_clean_attention`) from the checkpoint's objective.
- Method presets `config/backend/megatron/dllm/bd/method/{ar,sdar,bd3lm,fastdllm_v2,llada2,mdlm,nld}.yaml`
  and `config/experiments/dllm/bd/qwen3_<size>_<method>.yaml` for 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B and 8B.
- Qwen3 HF <-> MegaDLMs conversion by template fill, with a GPU parity check against HF
  (`convert/`, `eval/parity_check.py`, `config/experiments/dllm/bd/convert_qwen3_<size>.yaml`).
- Evaluation: offline NELBO (M1), GSM8K 4-shot with static and dynamic block decoding (M2, M3),
  a result collector, and a one-GPU chain (`eval/eval_chain.sh`, `eval_qwen3.yaml`).
- Native Snellius stack (no container): torch 2.13.0+cu126, Transformer Engine 2.16.0 built
  against it, transformers 5.14.1 (`oellm_autoexp/dllm/requirements-native-snellius.txt`,
  `build_native_stack_snellius.sbatch`, `config/{container,slurm}/snellius_megadlm_native.yaml`).
- Ablation configs: throughput probes, tier 0 (learning rate) and tier 1 (R00-R11) sweeps; no tier 2
  (human decision).
- Guard tests: every flag that a dllm experiment emits is checked against the launcher's argparser
  (I9, now also in the `megatron-extras` CI job), every bd job sets every `--bd-*` flag explicitly,
  the flags of every tier job match its run name, and every dllm experiment config composes.
- Branch history: `feat/megadlm` with `origin/main` merged in.

nodes.title: `nvidia-modelopt` missing on LUMI: Megatron-Bridge conversion fails with `No module named 'modelopt'`
nodes.description:
### Problem
Converting a checkpoint with the `megatron_bridge` backend on LUMI fails before conversion starts.
Megatron-Bridge's `AutoBridge`, which `run_export.py` uses, imports `nvidia-modelopt` at module level:

https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/0dae728241d4ead96c5da7aba7d2a383e58bf7d7/src/megatron/bridge/models/conversion/auto_bridge.py#L34

The LUMI training container (`config/container/lumi.yaml`) doesn't have it. With the fork and
Megatron-Bridge on `PYTHONPATH`:

```
  File ".../submodules/Megatron-Bridge/src/megatron/bridge/models/conversion/auto_bridge.py", line 34, in <module>
    from modelopt.torch.quantization.utils import is_quantized
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'modelopt'
```

`docs/bridge_eval_setup.md` says the convert stage reuses the training container and doesn't need a
separate one:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/docs/bridge_eval_setup.md#L23-L24

On JUPITER that's covered by a dedicated recipe, `MegatronTraining-JUPITER-bridge.def.in`, which adds
Bridge's extra dependencies, including `nvidia-modelopt`:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/container/megatron/MegatronTraining-JUPITER-bridge.def.in#L65-L76

LUMI has no equivalent recipe. (The guide notes that the LUMI chain was only checked with `--dry-run`,
which may be why this didn't show up earlier.)

We ran into this with the standard LUMI setup, when converting the checkpoints of our training runs.
We built our container from the repo's own recipe, `MegatronTrainingLumi.def.in`, with the documented
command from `container/README.md`, and conversion failed with the error above. The image that
`config/container/lumi.yaml` points to, built from the same recipe, fails the same way.

### Affected files
- `container/megatron/MegatronTrainingLumi.def.in`: the LUMI recipe, without Bridge's dependencies
- `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md` (L23–L24): "does not require a separate container"

### Our workaround
We built a separate conversion image by hand, in two steps. It isn't reproducible from the repo.

1. A training image from the repo's LUMI recipe, `MegatronTrainingLumi.def.in` (the same recipe as
   the image in `config/container/lumi.yaml`), with the documented LUMI build command from
   `container/README.md`:

   ```bash
   python ./container/build_container_user.py --backend megatron --definition MegatronTrainingLumi \
       --requirements container/megatron/requirements_latest.txt --output ./artifacts
   ```

2. That image unpacked into a sandbox, `nvidia-modelopt` added, and repacked. `pulp` is listed only
   because `--no-deps` skips `nvidia-modelopt`'s own dependencies, and `pulp` is one of them:

   ```bash
   SB=/tmp/$USER-sandbox   # local disk: the unpacked image has too many files for the scratch quota
   singularity build --sandbox --fix-perms $SB artifacts/MegatronTrainingLumi_x86_64.sif
   umask 022; singularity exec --writable --no-home --no-umask $SB \
       python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps nvidia-modelopt pulp
   chmod -R a+rX $SB/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/{modelopt,pulp,nvidia_modelopt-*,pulp-*}
   singularity build artifacts/MegatronTrainingLumi_bridge_x86_64.sif $SB && rm -rf $SB
   ```

   The conversion jobs then use this image (`container.image`) instead of the training image.

### Possible fix
- A LUMI bridge recipe (or a build option for `MegatronTrainingLumi.def.in`) that installs Bridge's
  extra dependencies the way the JUPITER bridge recipe does.

nodes.title: LUMI launcher drops `backend.env`, so Megatron-Bridge conversion silently uses Bridge's vendored Megatron-LM
nodes.description:
**Summary:** on LUMI, the `backend.env.PYTHONPATH` that points the conversion job at the OpenEuroLLM
Megatron-LM fork never reaches the container, so conversion silently uses the Megatron-LM bundled
inside Megatron-Bridge (megatron-core 0.18) instead of the fork the model was trained with.

A checkout of `main` contains two Megatron-LMs: the OpenEuroLLM fork as the repo's own submodule, and
the copy that Megatron-Bridge (also a submodule) ships in its `3rdparty/` folder:

| Megatron-LM | Path | Commit on `main` | megatron-core | Meant for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenEuroLLM fork | `submodules/Megatron-LM` | `bb5febb` | 0.16.0rc0 | training and conversion |
| Megatron-Bridge's bundled copy | `submodules/Megatron-Bridge/3rdparty/Megatron-LM` | `e41b370` | 0.18.0 | last-resort fallback for conversion |

### Background: `run_export.py`
The `megatron_bridge` backend converts a Megatron checkpoint to HuggingFace format. Its SLURM job runs
`python -m oellm_autoexp.backends.megatron_bridge.run_export …` inside the training container.
`run_export.py` first decides which Megatron-LM to import, in a documented order: the OpenEuroLLM
fork if it's on `PYTHONPATH`, otherwise one installed in the container, and only as a last resort
Megatron-Bridge's vendored copy (`3rdparty/Megatron-LM`):

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/backends/megatron_bridge/run_export.py#L209-L223

### Problem
On LUMI, the fork is configured with `backend.env.PYTHONPATH`, as the reference config does and the
comment in `lumi_bridge.yaml` describes:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/experiments/korbi/chain_qwen3_bridge_train_eval_lumi.yaml#L90

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_bridge.yaml#L5-L7

But `backend.env` never reaches the container. On SLURM, `backend.env` is only applied by the slurm
config's `launcher_cmd`, and the other launchers pass it to the container explicitly, e.g.
`juwels_bridge.yaml`:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/juwels_bridge.yaml#L14

`lumi.yaml`'s launcher, which `lumi_bridge.yaml` reuses unchanged, has no such part:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi.yaml#L6-L10

A `--dry-run` of the reference config shows it. Below is the command in the rendered conversion job
script that starts the container. Unmarked lines are what it renders today. The `+` lines are what it
renders with `backend.env` added to `lumi.yaml`'s launcher (see "Possible fix"); today they're missing,
and `PYTHONPATH` appears nowhere in the script:

```diff
 singularity exec \
+ --env HF_HOME=<HF_HOME> \
+ --env PYTHONPATH=/workspace/oellm-autoexp/submodules/Megatron-LM:/workspace/oellm-autoexp:/workspace/oellm-autoexp/submodules/Megatron-Bridge/src \
  --bind /pfs/ \
  --bind /scratch/ \
  --bind /flash/ \
  --bind $HOME \
  --bind $HOME/Projects/oellm-autoexp:/workspace/oellm-autoexp \
  <container>.sif python -m oellm_autoexp.backends.megatron_bridge.run_export --megatron-path …
```

For comparison, the eval job of the same chain uses `lumi_eval.yaml`, whose launcher does include
`backend.env`, and its `singularity exec` line has `--env …` options.

The LUMI training container doesn't ship Megatron-LM, so `import megatron.core` fails and
`run_export.py` falls back to Bridge's vendored copy (megatron-core 0.18) without any message:

```python
    try:
        import megatron.core  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:
        thirdparty = bridge_root / "3rdparty" / "Megatron-LM"
        if str(thirdparty) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(thirdparty))
```

So conversion runs with a different Megatron-LM than training. If the checkpoint was written by a newer
Megatron-LM than 0.18, conversion fails with `common.pt does not exist`, which is how we noticed.
Nothing in the log says which Megatron-LM was used, so this was hard to find.

Training on LUMI isn't affected, because it runs `./submodules/Megatron-LM/pretrain_gpt.py` directly
and Python finds the fork next to the script. (The LUMI chain in `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md` was only
checked with `--dry-run`, which may be why this didn't show up earlier.)

We ran into this when converting the checkpoints of our training runs on LUMI.

### Affected files
- [`config/slurm/lumi.yaml` L6–L10](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi.yaml#L6-L10): `launcher_cmd` without `backend.env`
- [`config/slurm/lumi_bridge.yaml` L5–L7](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_bridge.yaml#L5-L7): the comment
- [`oellm_autoexp/backends/megatron_bridge/run_export.py` L218–L223](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/backends/megatron_bridge/run_export.py#L218-L223): the silent fallback

### Our workaround
We put `PYTHONPATH` into `slurm.env` as `SINGULARITYENV_PYTHONPATH`. `lumi.yaml` exports every
`slurm.env` variable before `singularity exec`, and Singularity passes `SINGULARITYENV_*` variables
into the container:

```yaml
slurm.env.SINGULARITYENV_PYTHONPATH: "${oc.env:PWD}/submodules/Megatron-LM:${oc.env:PWD}:${oc.env:PWD}/submodules/Megatron-Bridge/src:/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages"
```

### Possible fix
- Pass `backend.env` in `lumi.yaml`'s launcher, as the other launchers do:

  ```diff
  -  ${oc.select:container.runtime,singularity} exec ${oc.join:' ',${oc.maptmpl:'--bind % \\\n',${container.bind}}} \
  +  ${oc.select:container.runtime,singularity} exec ${oc.join:' ',${oc.mapkeyvaltmpl:'--env %k=%v \\\n',${backend.env}}} ${oc.join:' ',${oc.maptmpl:'--bind % \\\n',${container.bind}}} \
  ```

  We checked this with a `--dry-run` only: the conversion job then gets the `+` lines shown above.
  Note that `lumi.yaml` is also the training launcher, so LUMI training jobs would then get their
  `backend.env` too (from `config/backend/megatron.yaml`: `PYTHONPATH=.:submodules/Megatron-LM`,
  `RUN_DIR`, `PROJECT_DIR`, plus `HF_HOME`). That's what those settings are meant to do, and the
  `PYTHONPATH` points at the same fork training already uses, but it hasn't been tested in a real run.
- `run_export.py`: log which `megatron.core` is used (path and version), and warn when falling back
  to the vendored copy.

### Possibly worth checking (not verified)
`lumi.yaml` is also the launcher for LUMI training, so any `backend.env` there is dropped as well, e.g.
`PYTHONPATH`, `PROJECT_DIR` and `RUN_DIR` from `config/backend/megatron.yaml`. Training works anyway (see
above), but other settings put in `backend.env` on LUMI would silently have no effect.

nodes.title: Fix `install_eval_env.sh --cluster lumi`
nodes.description:
Fixes the eight problems described in #73, which explains each one (where, what happens, why).
In short:

| # | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The env (~40k files) doesn't fit the LUMI home quota (100k files). | Optional `EVAL_LOCAL_DIR` (e.g. on scratch); `$HOME/eval_local` becomes a symlink to it. A non-empty `$HOME/eval_local` is never replaced. |
| 2 | `oellm-autoexp` and `lm-eval[math]` pin different `antlr4-python3-runtime` versions (4.9 vs 4.11). | Install only `oellm-eval[eval-base]`; the eval job doesn't need `oellm-autoexp`. |
| 3 | Editable installs write a `.pth` file, which Python ignores in a directory that's only on `PYTHONPATH`. | Non-editable install. |
| 4 | Newer `huggingface-hub` / `numpy` in the target dir shadow the container's; its `transformers` needs `huggingface-hub<1.0`, its `numba` needs `numpy<2.3`. | Install with constraints generated from the container's `pip list`. |
| 5 | No `oellm-eval` command: a dependency (`rouge`) installs a `bin` package where `--target` puts console scripts. | Write the `eval_local/bin/oellm-eval` entry point in the script. |
| 6 | oellm-eval runs `python`, but `lumi_eval.yaml`'s `PATH` override (host `PATH`) drops the container's `/opt/venv/bin`. | The stub venv gets a `python` wrapper running `/opt/venv/bin/python3`, and an `activate` that puts it on `PATH`. |
| 7 | `--prefetch` calls `scripts/prefetch_datasets.py`, which was never committed. | LUMI `--prefetch` uses `oellm-eval schedule --download_only true`. |
| 8 | Helper scripts run with the system `python3` (3.6 on LUMI) and fail with `SyntaxError`. | Run them via `uv run --python 3.12 python`. |

Also:
- `compoconf==0.1.14` → `compoconf>=0.2.2` in the leonardo and juwels/jupiter branches. Since
  2c5a309cf8589826144321863b3df197cc05df29 `pyproject.toml` requires `compoconf>=0.2.2`, so the old
  pin can't be installed together with `oellm-autoexp`.
- `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md`: the LUMI section showed the old manual install (editable,
  unconstrained). It now lists what the installer does on LUMI and why.

### Changed files
- `scripts/install_eval_env.sh` (incl. its header comment, which still described the LUMI install as editable)
- `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md` (LUMI section)

### Testing
On LUMI, fresh `bash scripts/install_eval_env.sh --cluster lumi` from this branch (with `main`'s
`oellm_evals` submodule) with `EVAL_LOCAL_DIR` on scratch: the env (~40k files) is installed there
behind the `$HOME/eval_local` symlink. Then, in the eval container started the way
`slurm/lumi_eval.yaml` does it (same `PYTHONPATH` / `PATH`):
- `oellm-eval --help` works (the written entry point);
- after `source ~/eval_venv_stub/bin/activate`, `python` runs `/opt/venv/bin/python3`, and
  `lm_eval` / `oellm` import from the installed env while `torch`, `transformers`, `numpy` and
  `huggingface_hub` stay the container's versions.

We also run our evaluation jobs on LUMI in an env installed this way.

Not tested: LUMI `--prefetch` (fix 7); leonardo / juwels / jupiter (only the `compoconf` pin changes
there). On `main` the installer's tokenizer download step still fails without `huggingface_hub`
(#72); the script reports it and continues.

Fixes #73

nodes.title: `install_eval_env.sh --cluster lumi` doesn't produce a working eval environment
nodes.description:
We set up checkpoint evaluation on LUMI with `scripts/install_eval_env.sh --cluster lumi`. The
resulting environment didn't work, for eight separate reasons. Links point to the current `main`.

As far as we can tell, this path hadn't been run end to end before: `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md` notes
that the LUMI chain was only checked with `--dry-run` because the project allocation was exhausted at
the time:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/docs/bridge_eval_setup.md#L205-L208

The guide's manual LUMI recipe ([L185–L203](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/docs/bridge_eval_setup.md#L185-L203))
does the same install as the script, so following it by hand gives the same result.

### Background: how the LUMI eval setup works
1. Eval jobs run inside a prebuilt container (`laif-rocm-….sif`) that has PyTorch, ROCm and
   `transformers` in `/opt/venv`, but not `oellm-eval` / `lm-eval`.
2. The container is read-only, and `pip install --user` is refused inside it (a venv is active).
3. So the script installs the extra packages into a plain directory with
   `pip install --target $HOME/eval_local/lib/python3.12/site-packages` ([L99–L108](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L99-L108)).
4. When an eval job starts, [`config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml` L15–L16](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml#L15-L16) starts the container with
   `PYTHONPATH=$HOME/eval_local/lib/python3.12/site-packages` and `PATH=$HOME/eval_local/bin:$PATH`,
   so Python in the container also finds those packages.

### 1. The environment doesn't fit in the LUMI home quota
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L99

- **What happens:** the installed env is ~40k files. The LUMI home quota is 100k files, and a home
  directory with a normal setup is already close to it (ours: 93k used, without the eval env).
- **Fix:** new optional `EVAL_LOCAL_DIR`. If set (e.g. to a directory on scratch), the env is
  installed there and `$HOME/eval_local` becomes a symlink to it, because `lumi_eval.yaml` hardcodes
  that path. An existing non-empty `$HOME/eval_local` is never replaced; the script stops with an error.

### 2. Dependency conflict between `oellm-autoexp` and `lm-eval`
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L106-L108

- **What happens:** `-e '$AUTOEXP_DIR'` installs `oellm-autoexp` next to `oellm-eval`.
  `oellm-autoexp` needs hydra / omegaconf, which pin `antlr4-python3-runtime==4.9.*`;
  `lm-eval[math]` pins `antlr4-python3-runtime==4.11`. Both can't be installed together.
- **Fix:** install only `oellm-eval[eval-base]`. The eval job only runs `oellm-eval schedule`; it
  doesn't need `oellm-autoexp`.

### 3. Editable installs are invisible via `PYTHONPATH`
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L106-L108

- **What happens:** `-e '$OELLM_EVALS_DIR[eval-base]'` is an editable install. An editable install doesn't copy the package. It writes a `.pth` file
  pointing at the source directory. Python only reads `.pth` files in its own site-packages
  directories, not in directories that are merely on `PYTHONPATH` (background step 4). So
  `import oellm` fails in the eval job.

  Editable installs do work on Leonardo, where the guide installs with `pip install --user -e`
  ([L153–L160](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/docs/bridge_eval_setup.md#L153-L160)):
  the user site directory is a site-packages directory, so its `.pth` files are read. The LUMI variant
  had to switch to `--target` (background step 2), and that's where it breaks.
- **Fix:** non-editable install, so the code is copied into the target directory.

### 4. Newer packages in the target directory break the container's packages
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L106

- **What happens:** pip resolves the dependencies without knowing about the container's packages and
  installs the newest versions into the target directory, e.g. `huggingface-hub` 1.x and a newer
  `numpy`. Because `PYTHONPATH` comes first, they shadow the container's versions, but the container's
  `transformers` requires `huggingface-hub<1.0` and its `numba` requires `numpy<2.3`.
- **Fix:** generate a constraints file from the container's `pip list` and install with `-c`, so the
  container's versions are kept.

### 5. No `oellm-eval` command
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L106

- **What happens:** [`lumi_eval.yaml` L16](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml#L16) expects the command in `$HOME/eval_local/bin`.
  With `--target`, pip puts console scripts into `<target>/bin`. A dependency
  (`rouge`) installs a Python package named `bin` (`bin/__init__.py`) into the same place, so the
  `oellm-eval` command isn't created where the job looks for it.
- **Fix:** the script writes a small `$HOME/eval_local/bin/oellm-eval` entry point itself.

### 6. `python` not found in the eval job
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L110-L113

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml#L16

- **What happens:** the script creates an empty stub venv `$HOME/eval_venv_stub/bin/activate`. oellm-eval's local mode runs `source $VENV/bin/activate; python -m lm_eval`. The
  container has `python` in `/opt/venv/bin`, but `lumi_eval.yaml` sets `--env PATH=$HOME/eval_local/bin:$PATH`,
  and `$PATH` is expanded **on the host**. Inside the container `PATH` is therefore the host's `PATH`,
  without `/opt/venv/bin`: `python` isn't found, and `python3` resolves to the container's
  `/usr/bin/python3`, which doesn't have the `/opt/venv` packages.
- **Fix:** the stub venv gets a `python` wrapper that runs `/opt/venv/bin/python3`, and an `activate`
  that puts the stub's `bin/` on `PATH`. A wrapper, not a symlink: a symlinked interpreter loses the
  `/opt/venv` site-packages.

### 7. `--prefetch` calls a script that was never committed
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L143-L148

- **What happens:** `scripts/prefetch_datasets.py` isn't in the repository, in any branch, although
  the [README (L135)](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/README.md#L135)
  recommends `install_eval_env.sh --prefetch` and the guide calls the script "the shipped helper"
  ([L100–L108](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/docs/bridge_eval_setup.md#L100-L108)).
- **Fix:** use oellm-eval's own `oellm-eval schedule ... --download_only true`.

### 8. Helper scripts fail with the system `python3`
https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L124-L130

- **What happens:** `patch_bridge_lazy_imports.py` and `download_tokenizers.py` run with `python3`.
  On LUMI login nodes, the system `python3` is 3.6. Both scripts start with
  `from __future__ import annotations` (Python ≥ 3.7) and fail with
  `SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined`. `download_tokenizers.py` would also need
  `huggingface_hub`.
- **Fix:** run them with `uv run --python 3.12 python ...`, in the repo environment.

### Other clusters
The [leonardo](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L71) and [juwels/jupiter](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/install_eval_env.sh#L84) branches pin `compoconf==0.1.14` and install
`oellm-autoexp` next to it. The pin matched `pyproject.toml` when the script was written, but
[2c5a309c](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/commit/2c5a309cf8589826144321863b3df197cc05df29)
raised the requirement to `compoconf>=0.2.2`, so pip can no longer satisfy both. The PR changes the
pin to `compoconf>=0.2.2` (not tested on those clusters).

### Affected files
- `scripts/install_eval_env.sh`
- `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md`: the LUMI section ([L185–L208](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/docs/bridge_eval_setup.md#L185-L208)) describes the old install
- related, unchanged: [`config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml` L15–L16](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml#L15-L16)

### Fix
Proposed in #74, as described per problem above.

### Possibly worth checking (not part of the fix, not verified)
- **Root cause of 6:** `lumi_eval.yaml` replaces the container's `PATH` with the host's. The PR works
  around it in the installer; fixing the launcher (e.g. not expanding `$PATH` on the host) might be

- **Why problem 1 needs a symlink:** `lumi_eval.yaml` hardcodes the env location as `$HOME/eval_local`
  (L15–L16). Making it a config value (e.g. `${oc.env:EVAL_LOCAL_DIR,${oc.env:HOME}/eval_local}`),
  used by both the launcher and the installer, would make the symlink unnecessary.
- Problem 7 is only fixed for LUMI. The leonardo and juwels/jupiter `--prefetch` branches, the usage
  text and `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md` still refer to the missing `scripts/prefetch_datasets.py`.
- Problems 2–5 are only fixed in the LUMI branch; we don't know whether the other branches have the
  same problems with editable installs and `--target` / `--user`.

nodes.title: Declare `huggingface_hub` as a dependency
nodes.description:

`scripts/download_tokenizers.py` imports `huggingface_hub`, but it isn't a declared dependency. It
only comes in through `transformers`, which is part of the optional `megatron` extra. After a plain
install it's missing, and the script fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` (e.g. the tokenizer download
step of `scripts/install_eval_env.sh`).

### Fix
Add `huggingface_hub>=0.30` to `[project] dependencies`.

### Changed files
- `pyproject.toml`

### Testing
Fresh virtualenv, plain install without extras (`uv pip install .`), then
`python scripts/download_tokenizers.py --tokenizers Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`:
- `main`: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'huggingface_hub'`
- this branch: `huggingface_hub` 2.3.0 is installed and the script downloads the tokenizer files.

Fixes #71

nodes.title: `huggingface_hub` is imported but not declared as a dependency
nodes.description:
### Problem
`scripts/download_tokenizers.py` imports `huggingface_hub`, but it isn't a declared dependency. The
only package that pulls it in is `transformers` (directly and via `tokenizers`), and `transformers`
is only in the optional `megatron` extra. So it's installed with the `megatron` extra, but **missing
after a plain install**, and the script fails:

```
    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'huggingface_hub'
```

(`oellm_autoexp/postprocess/converters/mcore_to_hf.py` imports it too, but that module also needs
`torch`, so it's only usable with the `megatron` extra, which brings `huggingface_hub` along.)

We ran into this when `scripts/install_eval_env.sh` failed at its tokenizer download step, which runs
`download_tokenizers.py` in the repo env.

### Affected files
- `pyproject.toml` (`[project] dependencies`)
- importers: [`scripts/download_tokenizers.py` L71–L72](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/download_tokenizers.py#L71-L72), [`oellm_autoexp/postprocess/converters/mcore_to_hf.py` L23](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/postprocess/converters/mcore_to_hf.py#L23)

### Fix
Proposed in #72: declare it.

```diff
   "tqdm>=4.65.0",
+  "huggingface_hub>=0.30",  # scripts/download_tokenizers.py, postprocess/converters/mcore_to_hf.py
 ]
```

`>=0.30` is the range we used (a fresh install currently resolves to 2.3.0). The APIs used
(`hf_hub_download`, `save_torch_state_dict`) exist since 0.23, but we haven't tested anything older.

nodes.title: Fix `monitor_autoexp.py --session` crashing without `--session-dir`
nodes.description:
### Problem
Reattaching to a session by name, `python scripts/monitor_autoexp.py --session <session_id>` as
documented in the README, crashed with `TypeError` when `--session-dir` wasn't given:

```python
session_dir = Path(args.session_dir) or Path(args.monitor_state_dir) / args.session
```

`Path(None)` raises before the `or` is evaluated. And since a `Path` is always truthy, the fallback to
`<monitor_state_dir>/<session>` could never be reached anyway.

### Fix
Use `--session-dir` if given, and otherwise derive the dir from `--monitor-state-dir` and `--session`:

```python
session_dir = Path(args.session_dir) if args.session_dir else Path(args.monitor_state_dir) / args.session
```

### Changed files
- `scripts/monitor_autoexp.py`
- `tests/monitor/test_monitor_autoexp_script.py`: regression test

### Testing
New tests run `main()` with monitoring stubbed out and check which state dir would be monitored:
- `--session <name>` → `<monitor-state-dir>/<name>`: fails without the fix (`TypeError`), passes with it.
- `--session-dir` takes precedence over `--session`: passes before and after.

`pytest tests/monitor`: 30 passed.

Fixes #69

nodes.title: `monitor_autoexp.py --session <id>` crashes with `TypeError` when `--session-dir` isn't given
nodes.description:
### Problem
Reattaching to a session by name, as `README.md` and `SPEC.md` document for resuming monitoring
after the monitor process died:

```bash
python scripts/monitor_autoexp.py --session <session_id>
```

crashes with:

```
TypeError: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'NoneType'
```

We ran into this when reattaching to a running session on LUMI.

### Cause
`scripts/monitor_autoexp.py`:

https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/monitor_autoexp.py#L106

That is:

```python
session_dir = Path(args.session_dir) or Path(args.monitor_state_dir) / args.session
```

When `--session-dir` isn't given, `args.session_dir` is `None` and `Path(None)` raises before the
`or` is evaluated. (Even with a value, a `Path` is always truthy, so the fallback could never be
reached.)

### Affected files
- [`scripts/monitor_autoexp.py` L106](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/scripts/monitor_autoexp.py#L106)

### Fix
Proposed in #70: check the argument itself, not the `Path`:

```diff
-    session_dir = Path(args.session_dir) or Path(args.monitor_state_dir) / args.session
+    session_dir = Path(args.session_dir) if args.session_dir else Path(args.monitor_state_dir) / args.session
```

The PR adds tests for which state dir is monitored: `--session` (fails without the fix) and
`--session-dir` taking precedence (unchanged).

### Possibly worth checking (not part of the fix, not verified)
If the session dir doesn't exist (e.g. a typo in the session name), the script prints
`Session directory … does not exist.`, then `JobFileStore` creates it empty ([`monitor/loop.py` L81](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/monitor/loop.py#L81))
and `run_loop` reports "All jobs finished." and exits with code 0 ([`orchestrator.py` L157–L160](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/orchestrator.py#L157-L160)).
The fix doesn't change this.

nodes.title: Fix argparse resolver leaking resolved values between sweep points
nodes.description:
### Problem
`argparse_resolver` (used by `oc.argsmegatron` / `oc.cliargs`) called `OmegaConf.resolve(args_dict)`,
which resolves the config **in place**: every interpolation is replaced by its value. The
hydra_staged_sweep repo cache (`hydra_staged_sweep/config/cache.py`) shares loaded config files
between compositions. The first sweep point's resolved values were therefore written into the shared
nodes, and every later sweep point read those values instead of evaluating its own interpolations.

It triggers when each sweep point selects its own config-group file and those files all include the
same shared file that holds the interpolation. For example, a sweep over `scale/small.yaml` and
`scale/large.yaml` where both include `base.yaml` with `save: ${job.base_output_dir}/checkpoints`:
all points then get the first point's `--save`, `--load`, tensorboard and wandb paths. No error is
raised. With the cache disabled (`HYDRA_STAGED_SWEEP_CACHE=0`) the output is correct.

**Note for users:** sweeps of this shape run before this fix may have written into the first sweep
point's directories.

### Fix
Use `OmegaConf.to_container(args_dict, resolve=True)`, which produces the same arguments without
modifying the config.

### Changed files
- `oellm_autoexp/argparse_schema/resolver.py`: resolve into a copy instead of in place
- `tests/hydra_staged_sweep/test_config_cache.py`: regression test
  `test_argparse_resolver_does_not_freeze_cached_interpolations`

### Testing
- The new test builds the layout above in a minimal config and composes it for two sweep points with
  the cache enabled. It fails without the fix (`/out/small/checkpoints != /out/large/checkpoints`)
  and passes with it.
- `pytest tests/hydra_staged_sweep/test_config_cache.py tests/argparse_schema`: 40 passed.
- `run_autoexp.py --dry-run` of a sweep over three model scales: without the fix all three rendered
  sbatch scripts have the first scale's `--save` path; with the fix each has its own.

Fixes #67

nodes.title: argparse resolver (`oc.argsmegatron` / `oc.cliargs`) leaks resolved values between sweep points
nodes.description:
### Problem
In a sweep whose points differ in a value that `backend.megatron` interpolates (e.g. a run dir per
model scale), every point after the first gets the **first point's** values in the
`oc.argsmegatron` / `oc.cliargs` output. No error, no warning.

We ran into this while running a sweep over three model scales: the second and third trainings were
generated with the first scale's run dir in `--save` / `--load`, the tensorboard and wandb paths, and
the data cache path.

### Cause
`argparse_resolver` calls `OmegaConf.resolve(args_dict)`, which resolves the node **in place**: each
interpolation is replaced by its value. The repo cache (`hydra_staged_sweep/config/cache.py`) shares
loaded config files between compositions, so the first sweep point's resolved values are written
into the shared nodes. An interpolation such as `save: ${job.base_output_dir}/checkpoints` is meant to
be evaluated by each sweep point with its own values; after the first point it has become a constant.
With the cache off (`HYDRA_STAGED_SWEEP_CACHE=0`) the output is correct.

**When it triggers:** each sweep point selects its own config-group file, and those files include the
**same shared file** that holds the interpolation. For example, the sweep selects `scale/small.yaml`
or `scale/large.yaml`, both include `base.yaml`, and `base.yaml` defines
`backend.megatron.save: ${job.base_output_dir}/checkpoints`. Simpler layouts (interpolation in the
primary config, or a plain value override per point) don't trigger it.

### Affected files
- [`oellm_autoexp/argparse_schema/resolver.py` L13–L17](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/argparse_schema/resolver.py#L13-L17)
- `oellm_autoexp/hydra_staged_sweep/config/cache.py` (`repo_cache`): shares the loaded nodes

### Fix
Proposed in #68: resolve into a copy instead of in place. `to_container(..., resolve=True)`
produces the same arguments without modifying the config:

```diff
     def argparse_resolver(args_dict: DictConfig) -> ListConfig:
-        OmegaConf.resolve(args_dict)
         return ListConfig(
             build_cmdline_args(
-                args=OmegaConf.to_container(args_dict),
+                args=OmegaConf.to_container(args_dict, resolve=True),
```

The PR adds a regression test that builds the layout above in a minimal config; it fails without
the fix and passes with it.

**Note for users:** sweeps of this shape run before the fix may have written into the first sweep
point's directories.

### Possibly worth checking (not part of the fix, not verified)
Three other resolvers in `oellm_autoexp/hydra_staged_sweep/config/resolvers.py` also call
`OmegaConf.resolve(inps)` in place: [`oc_kvmap_template`](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/hydra_staged_sweep/config/resolvers.py#L167-L168) (`oc.mapkeyvaltmpl`),
[`oc_valuemap_template`](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/hydra_staged_sweep/config/resolvers.py#L174-L175) and [`oc_map_extract_key`](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/oellm_autoexp/hydra_staged_sweep/config/resolvers.py#L179-L180). We haven't tested whether they leak
in the same layout. For example, [`config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/c6d0cc01660edb5bc401fe858715e0393906b6a2/config/slurm/lumi_eval.yaml#L14) applies `oc.mapkeyvaltmpl` to
`${backend.env}`.

nodes.title: Submodule clone fails on hosts without a GitHub SSH key: inconsistent SSH/HTTPS URLs in .gitmodules
nodes.description:
.gitmodules mixes SSH and HTTPS remote URLs across submodules:

- submodules/Megatron-LM → https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/NVIDIA-Megatron-LM.git (HTTPS)
- submodules/Megatron-Bridge → git@github.com:NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge.git (SSH)
- submodules/oellm_evals → git@github.com:OpenEuroLLM/oellm-evals.git (SSH)
- submodules/titan-oellm → git@github.com:OpenEuroLLM/titan-oellm.git (SSH)

git clone --recurse-submodules succeeds for the main repo and for Megatron-LM, but fails for the other three with:

```
git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
fatal: clone of 'git@github.com:NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge.git' into submodule path 'submodules/Megatron-Bridge' failed
```

All three of these repos (NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge, OpenEuroLLM/oellm-evals, OpenEuroLLM/titan-oellm) are public and readable anonymously over HTTPS, so there's no access-control reason for them to require SSH — it just breaks the clone for anyone who hasn't set up a GitHub SSH key on that particular machine.

**Suggested fix:** switch these three submodule URLs in .gitmodules to https://github.com/... form, consistent with Megatron-LM. 

Workaround for now, users hitting this can run before cloning:

```
git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf "git@github.com:"
```

nodes.description:
# Standalone checkpoint conversion + HF Hub upload tooling

## Summary

Adds a reusable, idempotent path for converting Megatron checkpoints from an
already-running training job to sharded HuggingFace format and publishing
them to a Hub repo (one branch per iteration), independent of the
orchestrator's train→convert→eval chain. Built and battle-tested end to end
converting and publishing all checkpoints from the OpenEuroLLM Prelude 9B
("baby") run (`openeurollm/prelude`, 280+ checkpoints so far).

## What's included

- `--max-shard-size` on `run_export.py` / `create_dummy_model.py`: the real
  export mirrors the dummy reference model's shard layout, so this has to be
  threaded through both. Defaults to `5GB`.
- `validate_export.py`: loads a converted checkpoint and runs a
  canonical-prompt, multilingual (36 EU languages) generation battery as a
  post-conversion smoke test, writing `validation.json` next to the
  checkpoint.
- `convert_and_validate_task.py`: single-checkpoint Slurm task entry point
  (convert + validate in-process), driven by a JSON manifest + task index.
- `scripts/mass_convert_checkpoints.py`: discovers unconverted checkpoints
  across one or more source dirs, batches them into Slurm jobs respecting a
  QOS's job cap, safe to re-run at any time (skips what's already done).
- `scripts/upload_to_hf.py`: pushes each converted checkpoint to its own Hub
  branch via `upload_large_folder` (resumable); a branch only counts as done
  once it actually has the weight files, not just because the ref exists.
- `docs/bridge_eval_setup.md`: new section documenting this path (setup
  prerequisites, example invocations, how it composes with a periodic
  watcher for ongoing incremental use).

## Why not part of the orchestrator chain

The chain in this doc assumes train/convert/eval are one managed pipeline
with a single output tree. This tooling targets a different, common case:
a training run is already in flight (or long finished), checkpoints exist
on disk, and the goal is "convert and publish everything, then keep up with
new ones as they land," independent of whether/how the run itself was
orchestrated.

## Testing

- End-to-end on Leonardo: full backfill of 280+ checkpoints, dependency
  pattern (conversion job → `sbatch --dependency=afterok` upload job) for
  incremental use, and the `--dry-run` catch-up scan, all verified against
  the live `openeurollm/prelude` repo.
- `python3.11 -m py_compile` on all changed/new files.

## Not included

- A periodic watcher/scheduler that invokes this tooling automatically as
  new checkpoints appear (that's a separate PR to `oellm-monitoring`, meant
  to run off-cluster so it isn't subject to login-node session limits).
- Any project-wide `uv.lock` changes (out of scope for this PR).

nodes.title: Some fixes for checkpoint conversion on Leonardo (Megatron -> HF)
nodes.description:
## Summary

Fixes several issues in the Megatron → HuggingFace checkpoint conversion (`megatron_bridge` backend) found while converting the Qwen3 dense `*_ne` models (0.1B–0.9B) on Leonardo. With these, all model sizes convert to structurally-correct, eval-ready HF checkpoints.

## Changes

- **Preserve tokenizer metadata** (`patch_tokenizer.py`): copy the canonical tokenizer files verbatim from the local tokenizer dir instead of re-serializing via `AutoTokenizer.save_pretrained`, which silently dropped metadata (`add_bos/eos_token`, `additional_special_tokens`, `added_tokens_decoder`, chat templates) that downstream eval harnesses rely on. Falls back to re-serialization only for remote HF-hub tokenizer ids.

- **GQA-aware HF config + checkpoint arch override** (`hf_config_gen.py`, `run_export.py`): `num_key_value_heads` is now derived correctly for both GQA and MHA models, and the core architecture fields (`num_layers`, `hidden_size`, `num_attention_heads`, `num_query_groups`, `kv_channels`, `ffn_hidden_size`) are overridden from the checkpoint's
  `modelopt_run_config.yaml` so a stale training-config snapshot can no longer produce a wrong `config.json` (previously the smaller no-GQA models exported an incorrect KV-head count).

- **Robust training-config resolver** (`resolvers.py`): new `oc.train_config` resolver to locate the Megatron training config used by `derive_hf_arch`. It honours an explicit filename, else a valid `current.yaml` symlink, else falls back to the newest `config-*.yaml`, so a broken/foreign `current.yaml` no longer breaks conversion.

- **Unique distributed port** (`run_export.py`): avoid a port collision when multiple conversion jobs land on the same node.

- **Example conversion config** (`config/experiments/swagatam/convert_0.9B_ne_leonardo.yaml`): a single-stage, fully-parameterized convert-only job (size / run / iter knobs) that derives all paths, for converting any checkpoint on Leonardo.

`--dry-run` exited immediately after building the execution plan, before any `.sbatch` scripts were generated. Users had no way to inspect rendered scripts without actually submitting jobs.

## Changes

- **`orchestrator.py`** — adds `render_scripts(plan: ExecutionPlan) -> list[Path]` that reuses `_build_job_record` to build each job's SLURM config and calls the existing `generate_script()` to write `.sbatch` files — no SLURM calls, no monitor-state files written. Non-SLURM (local) jobs are skipped with a debug log.
- **`run_autoexp.py`** — calls `render_scripts(plan)` in the `--dry-run` block before exiting.
- **`tests/integration/test_basic_flow.py`** — adds `test_render_scripts_dry_run` verifying that script files are created on disk for each job in the plan.

## Usage

```bash
# Renders .sbatch scripts to the configured script_dir, then exits — no jobs submitted
python scripts/run_autoexp.py --dry-run
```

nodes.title: Save checkpoints at specific steps
nodes.description:
The main branch of Megatron-LM now supports saving checkpoints at [specific steps](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/NVIDIA-Megatron-LM/pull/2), but it is not supported yet in `oellm-autoexp`. It is useful to start decay runs exactly from the saved steps' checkpoints.

The modification to Megatron-LM is adding the `--save-extra-steps` argument and this 1-liner:
```
  if args.save and args.save_interval and \
      (iteration % args.save_interval == 0 or \
      iteration in set(args.save_extra_steps)):
```
This PR adds the necessary changes to `oellm-autoexp` to use this argument. I give an example use in a config in my branch [here](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/exp_swagatam/config/experiments/swagatam/test_moe_80M_200MT_extra_checkpointing.yaml#L138). Instead of monitoring `start_iter_round`, with this the decay jobs can directly start from the calculated `start_iter` in the job starting [condition](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/blob/exp_swagatam/config/experiments/swagatam/test_moe_80M_200MT_extra_checkpointing.yaml#L216).

We also need to update the [submodule](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/oellm-autoexp/tree/main/submodules) to the current [main](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/NVIDIA-Megatron-LM) branch of Megatron-LM to use this feature.

nodes.title: Postprocessing: ckpt conversion + eval
nodes.description: Added a postprocess pipeline that runs torch_dist -> torch -> HF conversion and eval sequentially within the same slurm job as training. Each step is a separate config-driven class that builds its own command and gets wrapped in apptainer exec by the orchestrator, so everything runs inside the container without needing python on the host. Training and conversion use the same megatron launch command but the orchestrator strips conversion-only flags from the training invocation to keep them cleanly separated. Also patched the Megatron submodule to fix a pytorch 2.5 regression where checkpoint metadata was getting partially dropped during save, which broke the conversion

nodes.description: Model configurations should ideally *not* include environment-specific variables. This way, model configurations can be shared frictionless between different environments/machines.

nodes.title: Implement bring-your-own-container
nodes.description: Some machines/experiments require a specific container to run. Ideally we should (at least in the README)  describe how to use your own container to run the experiments, and even recommend this as a best practice.  Probably the container/environment to run the tool itself could be made leaner as well by implementing this.

nodes.title: Add default immutable machine configuration
nodes.description:
Some configuration settings should be immutable on specific machines. If these settings would (accidentally) be overridden, this could cause errors.
We should make it possible in the machine config to set highest-priority settings, so that machine defaults are not overridden on accident. When a setting is attempted to be overridden, a warning message should appear to notify the user.

oellm_autoexp.config.loader.ConfigLoaderError: Unable to parse config config/experiments/megatron_lumi_speed_test.yaml: Undefined keys {'defaults'} in data at key  for <class 'oellm_autoexp.config.schema.RootConfig'>: ['class_name', 'project', 'sweep', 'slurm', 'monitoring', 'backend', 'container', 'scheduler', 'metadata']
`

Suggestion:

Implement a sanity check that the file path is given correctly so that the parsing logic is robust.
